docs.title: nowcasteval
docs.text:
Score sample and quantile forecasts, and compare models against a baseline.

nowcasteval is the package in packages/nowcasteval of the repository, and builds on nowcastutils (Packages).

docs.title: Install
docs.text: uv pip install "git+https://github.com/seabbs/bdbv-hub-modelling#subdirectory=packages/nowcasteval"

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
We score a sample forecast of one count with the CRPS, the weighted interval score (WIS) and interval coverage.

import numpy as np

from nowcasteval.scoring import (
    coverage_sample,
    crps_sample,
    wis_quantile,
)

rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
samples = rng.poisson(20, size=1000)
observed = 18

crps = crps_sample(observed, samples)
covered = coverage_sample(observed, samples, level=0.9)
levels = np.array([0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95])
wis = wis_quantile([observed], np.quantile(samples, levels)[None, :], levels)
assert covered
assert np.isclose(
    wis["wis"][0],
    wis["dispersion"][0] + wis["overprediction"][0] + wis["underprediction"][0],
)

The CRPS is the fair form, whose expectation does not depend on the number of samples. The WIS comes with its three parts, dispersion, overprediction and underprediction, which sum to it.

docs.title: Score a table of forecasts
docs.text:
score_forecasts scores one row per sample against the observed counts, on the natural and log scales. relative_skill divides each model's mean score by a baseline's, on the forecasts both made.

import pandas as pd

from nowcasteval.scoring import relative_skill, score_forecasts

rows = []
for model, rate in (("baseline", 20), ("candidate", 17)):
    for week in ("2026-01-10", "2026-01-17"):
        for i, value in enumerate(rng.poisson(rate, 100)):
            rows.append(
                {
                    "model": model,
                    "kind": "real",
                    "vintage": "2026-01-05",
                    "reference_date": "2026-01-10",
                    "location": "A",
                    "target_end_date": week,
                    "horizon": 0,
                    "sample": i,
                    "value": value,
                }
            )
forecasts = pd.DataFrame(rows)
truth = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "location": ["A", "A"],
        "target_end_date": ["2026-01-10", "2026-01-17"],
        "truth": [16, 18],
    }
)
scores = score_forecasts(forecasts, truth)
skill = relative_skill(scores, baseline="baseline")
assert {"wis", "log_wis", "crps", "coverage_90"} <= set(scores.columns)
assert skill.set_index("model").loc["baseline", "relative_wis"] == 1.0

docs.title: Score a joint forecast of several places
docs.text:
energy_sample scores samples of a vector, such as the same week in several places, so that a forecast is rewarded for getting their dependence right.

from nowcasteval.scoring import energy_sample

joint = rng.poisson([20, 5], size=(1000, 2))
energy = energy_sample([18, 7], joint)
assert energy > 0

docs.title: nowcasteval.scoring
docs.text:
Score sample forecasts.

Scores follow scoringutils conventions, as in epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize (src/scoring.jl).

  • WIS from the sample quantiles at QUANTILE_LEVELS (the 23 levels the US hubs use). With $K$ central intervals plus the median, written as quantile levels $\tau$ with sample quantiles $q_\tau$, $$\text{WIS}(F, y) = \frac{1}{K + 1/2}\sum_\tau \left(\mathbb{1}{y < q_\tau} - \tau\right)(q_\tau - y),$$ which equals the usual interval form: half the median's absolute error plus scoringrules' interval_score of each central interval, weighted by $\alpha / 2$. Our vectorised code computes it with its split into dispersion, overprediction and underprediction, which scoringrules lacks. wis_quantile gives the same for forecasts made as quantiles, and score_quantiles scores those by WIS, the absolute error of the median and the coverage of each central interval.
  • Log WIS: WIS of $\log(1 + y)$ against $\log(1 + x)$ for the samples.
  • CRPS in the fair form (Ferro 2014) over $m$ samples, $$\frac{1}{m}\sum_i |x_i - y| - \frac{1}{2m(m - 1)}\sum_{i \ne j} |x_i - x_j|,$$ scoringrules' crps_ensemble with estimator="fair", as the paper scores. Its expectation does not depend on $m$, so forecasts with different numbers of draws compare. estimator="nrg" gives the CRPS of the empirical distribution. The BDBV pages score by CRPS, as the hub takes samples; the German benchmark scores quantiles by WIS.
  • Log CRPS: CRPS of $\log(1 + y)$ against $\log(1 + x)$. It scores relative error, so large provinces do not dominate.
  • Coverage of the central 50% and 90% sample intervals.
  • Bias $1 - (P(X \le y) + P(X \le y - 1))$ for counts, in $[-1, 1]$. Positive means overprediction.
  • Energy score of a vector forecast, in the fair form over $m$ samples, $$\text{ES}(F, \mathbf{y}) = \frac{1}{m}\sum_i |\mathbf{X}_i - \mathbf{y}|
  • \frac{1}{2m(m-1)}\sum_{i \ne j} |\mathbf{X}_i - \mathbf{X}_j|,$$ scoringrules' es_ensemble with estimator="fair". The vector is every place at one scale by every scored week, for one origin, so the score rewards getting the joint pattern right. The sample index is the joint draw.
  • Log energy score: the energy score of $\log(1 + \mathbf{y})$ against $\log(1 + \mathbf{X})$.

relative_skill divides a model's mean score by the baseline's mean score over the forecasts both made. pairwise_skill is scoringutils' pairwise relative skill, for models that forecast different targets: each pair's mean score ratio on the forecasts both made, a model's geometric mean of its ratios, scaled to a reference model.

def wis_sample(
    obs: float,
    samples: ArrayLike,
    quantile_levels: NDArray[np.float64] = QUANTILE_LEVELS,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Return the WIS of a sample forecast and its components.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : float
        The observed value.
    samples : array-like
        Sample values.
    quantile_levels : numpy.ndarray
        Symmetric quantile levels including 0.5.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `wis`, `dispersion`, `overprediction` and `underprediction`.
        The components sum to `wis`.
    """
    x = _as_samples(samples)
    tau = np.asarray(quantile_levels, dtype=np.float64)
    out = wis_quantile(np.array([obs]), np.quantile(x, tau)[None, :], tau)
    return {k: float(v[0]) for k, v in out.items()}

def wis_quantile(
    obs: ArrayLike, quantiles: ArrayLike, quantile_levels: ArrayLike
) -> dict[str, NDArray[np.float64]]:
    """Return the WIS of quantile forecasts and its components.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : array-like
        The observed values, `[N]`.
    quantiles : array-like
        Each forecast's quantiles at `quantile_levels`, `[N, K]`.
    quantile_levels : array-like
        Symmetric quantile levels including 0.5, ascending, `[K]`.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `wis`, `dispersion`, `overprediction` and `underprediction`, each
        `[N]`. The components sum to `wis`.
    """
    y = np.asarray(obs, dtype=np.float64)[:, None]
    q = np.asarray(quantiles, dtype=np.float64)
    tau = np.asarray(quantile_levels, dtype=np.float64)
    lower = tau < 0.5
    # Pair each lower level with its upper level.
    lo, hi = q[:, lower], q[:, tau > 0.5][:, ::-1]
    alpha = 2 * tau[lower]
    med = q[:, np.isclose(tau, 0.5)]
    disp = np.sum(alpha / 2 * (hi - lo), axis=1)
    over = np.sum(np.maximum(lo - y, 0), axis=1)
    over += np.maximum(med - y, 0)[:, 0] / 2
    under = np.sum(np.maximum(y - hi, 0), axis=1)
    under += np.maximum(y - med, 0)[:, 0] / 2
    norm = lower.sum() + 0.5
    return {
        "wis": (disp + over + under) / norm,
        "dispersion": disp / norm,
        "overprediction": over / norm,
        "underprediction": under / norm,
    }

def crps_sample(
    obs: float, samples: ArrayLike, estimator: str = "fair"
) -> float:
    r"""Return the CRPS of a sample forecast.

    $\frac{1}{m}\sum_i |x_i - y| - \frac{1}{2c}\sum_{i, j} |x_i - x_j|$,
    with the pair sum in sorted closed form. The fair form (Ferro 2014)
    has $c = m(m - 1)$ and an expectation that does not depend on $m$;
    `nrg`, the CRPS of the empirical distribution, has $c = m^2$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : float
        The observed value.
    samples : array-like
        Sample values.
    estimator : str
        `"fair"`, as scoringrules' `crps_ensemble(estimator="fair")`, or
        `"nrg"`.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The CRPS. With one sample the fair form has no spread term.
    """
    if estimator not in ("fair", "nrg"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"estimator must be 'fair' or 'nrg', not {estimator!r}."
        )
    x = _as_samples(samples)
    y = np.array([obs], dtype=np.float64)
    return float(crps_ensemble(y, x[None, :], estimator)[0])

def crps_ensemble(
    obs: ArrayLike, samples: ArrayLike, estimator: str = "fair"
) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Return the CRPS of many sample forecasts at once.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : array-like
        The observed values, `[N]`.
    samples : array-like
        Each forecast's draws, `[N, m]`.
    estimator : str
        `"fair"` or `"nrg"`, as `crps_sample`.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        The CRPS of each forecast, `[N]`: scoringrules' `crps_ensemble`,
        the fair form through its `pwm` estimator (`_crps`).
    """
    y = np.asarray(obs, dtype=np.float64)
    x = np.asarray(samples, dtype=np.float64)
    if estimator == "fair":
        return _crps(y, x)
    if estimator == "nrg":
        return np.asarray(
            sr.crps_ensemble(y, x, m_axis=-1, estimator="nrg"),
            dtype=np.float64,
        ).reshape(y.shape)
    raise ValueError(f"estimator must be 'fair' or 'nrg', not {estimator!r}.")

def scale_of(location: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """Return `national`, `provinces` or `zones` for each location code.

    Parameters
    ----------
    location : pandas.Series
        Location codes, such as `CD`, `CD-IT` and `CD-IT-10`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.Series
        The scale of each code.
    """
    depth = location.str.count("-")
    return depth.map({0: "national", 1: "provinces"}).fillna("zones")

def energy_scores(
    samples: pd.DataFrame,
    truth: pd.DataFrame,
    unit: Sequence[str],
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score every model's joint forecast of each scale with the energy score.

    Within one `unit` and scale, the vector is the place-week cells that
    every model in the unit forecasts and the truth has. Each model's
    samples are its rows with the same `sample` index.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        The `unit` columns, `model`, `location`, `target_end_date`,
        `sample` and `value`.
    truth : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `truth`, plus any
        columns it should be matched on.
    unit : sequence of str
        Columns that identify one forecast of every scale, such as an
        origin and the release scored against.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per unit, `scale` and `model`: `n_cells`, `n_samples`,
        `energy` and `log_energy`.
    """
    unit = list(unit)
    cell = ["location", "target_end_date"]
    on = [c for c in truth.columns if c != "truth"]
    rows = samples.merge(truth, on=on)
    rows["scale"] = scale_of(rows["location"])
    out: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for key, grp in rows.groupby([*unit, "scale"], sort=True):
        have = grp[["model", *cell]].drop_duplicates()
        count = have.groupby(cell).size()
        shared = count[count == have["model"].nunique()].index
        grp = grp.set_index(cell).loc[shared].reset_index()
        y = grp.drop_duplicates(cell).set_index(cell)["truth"]
        for model, own in grp.groupby("model"):
            x = own.pivot(index="sample", columns=cell, values="value")
            x = x.astype(float)
            obs = y.reindex(x.columns).to_numpy(dtype=float)
            out.append(
                {
                    **dict(zip([*unit, "scale"], key, strict=True)),
                    "model": model,
                    "n_cells": x.shape[1],
                    "n_samples": x.shape[0],
                    "energy": energy_sample(obs, x),
                    "log_energy": energy_sample(np.log1p(obs), np.log1p(x)),
                }
            )
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

def coverage_sample(obs: float, samples: ArrayLike, level: float) -> bool:
    """Whether the observation is inside the central sample interval.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : float
        The observed value.
    samples : array-like
        Sample values.
    level : float
        Interval width, such as 0.5 or 0.9.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if the observation is inside, bounds included.
    """
    x = _as_samples(samples)
    lo, hi = np.quantile(x, [(1 - level) / 2, (1 + level) / 2])
    return bool(lo <= obs <= hi)

def bias_sample(obs: float, samples: ArrayLike) -> float:
    r"""Return the bias of a sample forecast of a count.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : float
        The observed count.
    samples : array-like
        Sample values.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        $1 - (P(X \le y) + P(X \le y - 1))$, in $[-1, 1]$. Positive
        means the forecast is too high.
    """
    x = _as_samples(samples)
    n_lt = np.sum(x < obs)
    n_eq = np.sum(x == obs)
    return float(1 - (2 * n_lt + n_eq) / x.size)

def score_sample(obs: float, samples: ArrayLike) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Return every score in `SCORE_COLUMNS` for one forecast.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : float
        The observed value.
    samples : array-like
        Sample values.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Scores keyed by `SCORE_COLUMNS`.
    """
    x = _as_samples(samples)
    out = wis_sample(obs, x)
    out["log_wis"] = wis_sample(float(np.log1p(obs)), np.log1p(x))["wis"]
    out["crps"] = crps_sample(obs, x)
    out["log_crps"] = crps_sample(float(np.log1p(obs)), np.log1p(x))
    out["ae_median"] = float(abs(np.median(x) - obs))
    out["coverage_50"] = float(coverage_sample(obs, x, 0.5))
    out["coverage_90"] = float(coverage_sample(obs, x, 0.9))
    out["bias"] = bias_sample(obs, x)
    return out

def score_cells(
    obs: ArrayLike,
    samples: ArrayLike,
    coverage: Sequence[int] = (50, 90),
) -> dict[str, NDArray[np.float64]]:
    """Return every score of many forecasts at once.

    The scores of `score_sample` for each row, computed on the whole
    array: WIS and log WIS from the sample quantiles, fair CRPS and log
    CRPS (scoringrules' `crps_ensemble`), the absolute error of the
    median, coverage and bias.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obs : array-like
        The observed values, `[N]`.
    samples : array-like
        Each forecast's draws, `[N, m]`.
    coverage : sequence of int
        Central interval widths in percent, each a `coverage_<p>` column.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `[N]` arrays keyed by `SCORE_COLUMNS` (with the `coverage`
        columns asked for).
    """
    y = np.asarray(obs, dtype=np.float64)
    x = np.asarray(samples, dtype=np.float64)
    if x.ndim != 2 or x.shape[1] == 0 or x.shape[0] != y.size:
        raise ValueError(f"Need [N, m] samples for N={y.size}, not {x.shape}.")
    tau = QUANTILE_LEVELS
    out = wis_quantile(y, np.quantile(x, tau, axis=1).T, tau)
    ly, lx = np.log1p(y), np.log1p(x)
    out["log_wis"] = wis_quantile(ly, np.quantile(lx, tau, axis=1).T, tau)[
        "wis"
    ]
    out["crps"] = _crps(y, x)
    out["log_crps"] = _crps(ly, lx)
    out["ae_median"] = np.abs(np.median(x, axis=1) - y)
    for p in coverage:
        level = p / 100
        lo, hi = np.quantile(x, [(1 - level) / 2, (1 + level) / 2], axis=1)
        out[f"coverage_{p}"] = ((lo <= y) & (y <= hi)).astype(np.float64)
    n_lt = np.sum(x < y[:, None], axis=1)
    n_eq = np.sum(x == y[:, None], axis=1)
    out["bias"] = 1 - (2 * n_lt + n_eq) / x.shape[1]
    return out

def score_forecasts(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    truth: pd.DataFrame,
    keys: Sequence[str] = (
        "model",
        "kind",
        "vintage",
        "reference_date",
        "location",
        "target_end_date",
    ),
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score sample forecasts against observed values.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        One row per sample, with the `keys` columns, `horizon`, `sample`
        and `value`.
    truth : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `truth`, plus any key
        columns it should be matched on (such as `kind` for simulated
        data).
    keys : sequence of str
        Columns that identify one forecast.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per forecast with a truth value: the keys, `horizon`,
        `truth`, `n_samples` and `SCORE_COLUMNS`.

    Examples
    --------
    Score against the latest release, with `forecasts` from `run_forecasts`.

    >>> from nowcastbdbv.data.tidy import load_target, vintages
    >>> from nowcasteval.scoring import (
    ...     score_forecasts, summarise_scores
    ... )
    >>> real = load_target().query("kind == 'real'")
    >>> latest = real.loc[real["vintage"] == vintages(real)[-1]]
    >>> truth = latest.rename(columns={"total": "truth"})[
    ...     ["location", "target_end_date", "truth"]
    ... ]
    >>> scores = score_forecasts(forecasts, truth)
    >>> summarise_scores(scores, by=["model"])
    """
    keys = [*keys, "horizon"]
    on = [c for c in truth.columns if c != "truth"]
    merged = forecasts.merge(truth, on=on, how="inner")
    if merged.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            columns=[*keys, "truth", "n_samples", *SCORE_COLUMNS]
        )
    group = merged.groupby(keys, sort=True)
    merged["_cell"] = group.ngroup()
    cells = group.agg(truth=("truth", "first"), n_samples=("value", "size"))
    cells = cells.reset_index()
    merged = merged.sort_values("_cell", kind="stable")
    parts = []
    # One array per draw count: cells with m draws form an [N, m] array.
    for _, idx in cells.groupby("n_samples").groups.items():
        sub = cells.loc[idx]
        values = merged.loc[merged["_cell"].isin(sub.index), "value"]
        draws = values.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64).reshape(len(sub), -1)
        scores = score_cells(sub["truth"].to_numpy(), draws)
        parts.append(sub.assign(**{c: scores[c] for c in SCORE_COLUMNS}))
    out = pd.concat(parts).sort_index()
    out["truth"] = out["truth"].astype(float)
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

def score_quantiles(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    truth: pd.DataFrame,
    keys: Sequence[str],
    quantile_levels: ArrayLike,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score quantile forecasts against observed values.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        One row per quantile, with the `keys` columns, `horizon`,
        `quantile` and `value`.
    truth : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `truth`, plus any key
        columns it should be matched on.
    keys : sequence of str
        Columns that identify one forecast.
    quantile_levels : array-like
        Symmetric quantile levels including 0.5. Every forecast must give
        each of them.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per forecast with a truth value: the keys, `horizon`,
        `truth`, the `wis_quantile` columns, `ae_median` and
        `coverage_<w>`, whether the truth is inside the central $w$%
        interval, bounds included, for each pair of levels.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a forecast lacks one of `quantile_levels`.
    """
    tau = np.sort(np.asarray(quantile_levels, dtype=np.float64))
    on = [c for c in truth.columns if c != "truth"]
    rows = forecasts.merge(truth, on=on, how="inner")
    rows = rows.assign(quantile=rows["quantile"].round(6))
    wide = rows.pivot_table(
        index=[*keys, "horizon", "truth"],
        columns="quantile",
        values="value",
        aggfunc="first",
    ).reindex(columns=tau.round(6))
    if wide.isna().to_numpy().any():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Each forecast needs the quantile levels {tau.tolist()}."
        )
    q = wide.to_numpy()
    y = wide.index.get_level_values("truth").to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    out = pd.DataFrame(wis_quantile(y, q, tau), index=wide.index)
    out["ae_median"] = np.abs(q[:, np.isclose(tau, 0.5)][:, 0] - y)
    for i in np.flatnonzero(tau < 0.5):
        width = round(100 * (1 - 2 * tau[i]))
        inside = (q[:, i] <= y) & (y <= q[:, -1 - i])
        out[f"coverage_{width}"] = inside.astype(float)
    return out.reset_index()

    """Average scores over forecasts within groups.

    by : sequence of str

    -------
    pandas.DataFrame

    out = grp[list(SCORE_COLUMNS)].mean()
    out.insert(0, "n", grp.size())
    return out.reset_index()

def relative_skill(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    baseline: str = "randomwalk",
    by: Sequence[str] = (),
    metrics: Sequence[str] = ("wis", "log_wis"),
    match_on: Sequence[str] = (
        "kind",
        "vintage",
        "reference_date",
        "location",
        "target_end_date",
    ),
    means: Sequence[str] = (),
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each model's mean score divided by the baseline's.

    Only forecasts made by both the model and the baseline are compared.
    Values below 1 mean the model beats the baseline.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `score_forecasts`.
    baseline : str
        The baseline model name.
    by : sequence of str
        Extra columns to compare within, such as `("horizon",)`.
    metrics : sequence of str
        Scores to compare.
    match_on : sequence of str
        Columns that identify the same forecast across models.
    means : sequence of str
        Columns to average over the same forecasts, for the model and the
        baseline.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model`, the `by` columns, `n`, each `means` column and
        its baseline mean `base_<column>`, and `relative_<metric>` for
        each metric: the model's mean over the baseline's, missing where
        the baseline's mean is 0. The baseline has 1.
    """
    match = list(dict.fromkeys([*match_on, *by]))
    cols = list(dict.fromkeys([*metrics, *means]))
    base = scores.loc[scores["model"] == baseline, [*match, *cols]]
    merged = scores.merge(base, on=match, suffixes=("", "_base"))
    group = ["model", *by]
    grp = merged.groupby(group)
    out = grp.size().rename("n").to_frame()
    for c in means:
        out[c] = grp[c].mean()
        out[f"base_{c}"] = grp[f"{c}_base"].mean()
    for m in metrics:
        num = grp[m].mean()
        den = grp[f"{m}_base"].mean()
        out[f"relative_{m}"] = num / den.where(den > 0)
    return out.reset_index()

def pairwise_skill(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    reference: str,
    by: Sequence[str] = (),
    metrics: Sequence[str] = ("wis", "log_wis"),
    match_on: Sequence[str] = (
        "kind",
        "vintage",
        "reference_date",
        "location",
        "target_end_date",
    ),
    rounds: str = "reference_date",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each model's pairwise relative skill, scaled to `reference`.

    As scoringutils' `get_pairwise_comparisons`: for each pair of
    models, the ratio of their summed scores on the forecasts both made;
    a model's skill is the geometric mean of its ratios against every
    model, itself (ratio 1) included; the scaled skill divides it by the
    reference's. Pairs with no forecasts in common are left out. Models
    can so be compared when they forecast different targets. Values
    below 1 mean the model beats the reference.

    Unlike scoringutils, a model that shares forecasts with no other
    model has no skill (rather than 1), unless it is the only model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        One row per model and forecast, with `model`, the `match_on` and
        `by` columns and each metric.
    reference : str
        The model the skills are scaled to.
    by : sequence of str
        Columns to compare within, such as `("horizon",)`.
    metrics : sequence of str
        Scores to compare, each on its own (such as WIS on the natural
        and on the log scale).
    match_on : sequence of str
        Columns that, with `by`, identify the same forecast across
        models (scoringutils' forecast unit without `model`).
    rounds : str
        The column whose distinct values are counted as each model's
        rounds.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model`, the `by` columns, `n` (the model's forecasts),
        `rounds` (its distinct `rounds` values), and for each metric
        `skill_<metric>` (the geometric mean) and `relative_<metric>`
        (scaled to the reference, which has 1; missing without the
        reference). Rows within each `by` group.
    """
    by = list(by)
    match = list(dict.fromkeys([*match_on, *by]))
    parts = scores.groupby(by) if by else [((), scores)]
    frames, keys = [], []
    for key, part in parts:
        grp = part.groupby("model")
        frame = grp.size().rename("n").to_frame()
        frame["rounds"] = grp[rounds].nunique()
        for m in metrics:
            wide = part.pivot_table(
                index=match, columns="model", values=m, aggfunc="first"
            )
            theta = _theta(wide)
            frame[f"skill_{m}"] = theta
            frame[f"relative_{m}"] = theta / theta.get(reference, np.nan)
        frames.append(frame)
        keys.append(key)
    if by:
        res = pd.concat(frames, keys=keys, names=by).reset_index()
    else:
        res = frames[0].reset_index()
    cols = ["model", *by, "n", "rounds"]
    return res[cols + [c for c in res.columns if c not in cols]]

docs.title: nowcasteval.backtest
docs.text:
Rolling-origin backtest over every real vintage.

Each vintage becomes a ForecastTask: the data as of that vintage, the reference date it serves (reference_date_for_vintage) and the weeks from min_horizon to max_horizon (the BDBV data's are built by nowcastbdbv.backtest.make_tasks). Every registered model forecasts every task. Real forecasts are scored by nowcasteval.nowcast on the count each later release reported.

Every origin but the latest is backtested: each real vintage with at least two usable releases up to it (backtest_origins). truth_changes shows how much the truth moved between vintages.

def load_config(
    path: Path | str = "packages/nowcastbdbv/config/backtest.toml",
) -> BacktestConfig:
    """Read the backtest settings.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        The TOML file.

    Returns
    -------
    BacktestConfig
        The settings.
    """
    raw = tomllib.loads(Path(path).read_text())
    fc, sp = raw["forecast"], raw["split"]
    return BacktestConfig(
        min_horizon=int(fc["min_horizon"]),
        max_horizon=int(fc["max_horizon"]),
        n_samples=int(fc["n_samples"]),
        score_samples=int(
            raw.get("samples", {}).get("backtest", fc["n_samples"])
        ),
        seed=int(fc["seed"]),
        complete_after_weeks=int(sp["complete_after_weeks"]),
        sampler=dict(raw["sampler"]),
        bvd_max_rhat=float(raw["bvd"]["max_rhat"]),
        max_delay=(
            int(fc["max_delay"]) if fc.get("max_delay") is not None else None
        ),
        truth_delay=_truth_delay(sp.get("truth_delay", "auto")),
        truth_level=_truth_level(sp.get("truth_level", TRUTH_LEVEL)),
    )

def forecast_weeks(
    reference_date: dt.date | str, config: BacktestConfig
) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return the weeks a forecast covers.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reference_date : datetime.date or str
        The reference date.
    config : BacktestConfig
        Gives the horizon range.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of str
        ISO Saturdays from `min_horizon` to `max_horizon`.
    """
    ref = as_date(reference_date)
    return tuple(
        (ref + dt.timedelta(weeks=h)).isoformat()
        for h in range(config.min_horizon, config.max_horizon + 1)
    )

def check_distinct(forecasts: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    """Stop if two models gave the same samples for a task.

    A model that silently ran another would give the same samples, as
    the daily random walk once did when it had no snapshots.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `run_forecasts` with `model`, `kind`, `vintage` and
        `value`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If two models have identical values for the same task.
    """
    for key, rows in forecasts.groupby(["kind", "vintage"]):
        seen: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        for name, grp in rows.groupby("model"):
            values = grp.sort_values(["location", "target_end_date", "sample"])[
                "value"
            ].to_numpy()
            for other, prior in seen.items():
                if prior.shape == values.shape and np.array_equal(
                    prior, values
                ):
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{name} and {other} gave identical samples for {key}."
                    )
            seen[str(name)] = values

def run_forecasts(
    models: Sequence[ForecastModel],
    tasks: Iterable[ForecastTask],
    fits: list[pd.DataFrame] | None = None,
    learnt: list[pd.DataFrame] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Run every model on every task, adding the national total.

    A model that raises `ModelUnavailableError` for a task, as the random
    walk models do when no pair of releases is within the delay window,
    has no rows for that task.
    A model with `needs_snapshots` set must be given the task's release
    snapshots, and the run stops if it is not.

    Parameters
    ----------
    models : sequence of ForecastModel
        Models to run.
    tasks : iterable of ForecastTask
        Tasks to run them on.
    fits : list, optional
        Collects a table of each model's fit summaries per task, for
        models that set `fit_diagnostics`.
    learnt : list, optional
        Collects each fit's learnt delay per task, for models that set
        `delay_summary`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model`, `kind`, `vintage`, `reference_date`, `horizon`,
        `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample`, `value` and `as_of`
        (missing for final counts).

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from nowcasteval.backtest import run_forecasts
    >>> from bdbvhub.models import get_model
    >>> models = [get_model("randomwalk"), get_model("randomwalknowcast")]
    >>> forecasts = run_forecasts(models, [task])  # e.g. nowcastbdbv make_tasks
    >>> forecasts.groupby("model")["sample"].nunique()
    """
    frames = []
    for task in tasks:
        for model in models:
            if getattr(model, "needs_snapshots", False) and (
                task.daily_history is None or task.daily_history.empty
            ):
                raise MissingSnapshots(
                    f"{model.name} needs daily release snapshots, and the "
                    f"{task.kind} task for {task.vintage} has none."
                )
            if hasattr(model, "fit_diagnostics"):
                model.fit_diagnostics = []
            try:
                samples = model.forecast(task)
            except ModelUnavailableError as err:
                log.warning(
                    "%s skipped %s %s: %s", model.name, task.kind,
                    task.vintage, err,
                )  # fmt: skip
                continue
            table = _fit_rows(model, task)
            if fits is not None and not table.empty:
                fits.append(table)
            delay = getattr(model, "delay_summary", None)
            if learnt is not None and delay is not None:
                learnt.append(delay)
            check_samples(samples, task)
            if "as_of" not in samples:
                samples["as_of"] = np.nan
            samples = add_national(samples)
            ref = pd.Timestamp(task.reference_date)
            samples["horizon"] = (
                pd.to_datetime(samples["target_end_date"]) - ref
            ).dt.days // 7
            samples.insert(0, "model", model.name)
            samples.insert(1, "kind", task.kind)
            samples.insert(2, "vintage", task.vintage)
            samples.insert(3, "reference_date", task.reference_date.isoformat())
            frames.append(samples)
    if not frames:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=FORECAST_COLUMNS).astype(_FORECAST_DTYPES)
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)

def merge_by_model(path: Path | str, new: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Merge a run's rows into a results file, keeping other models' rows.

    The fitted variants are slow, so their rows come from the fit store
    (`bdbvhub.store.store`). A run replaces the rows of the
    models it ran and keeps the rest, so a run of no model keeps them all.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        A results file with a `model` column. It need not exist.
    new : pandas.DataFrame
        The run's rows.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The kept rows of other models, then `new`.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if not path.exists():
        return new
    # An empty table still has a gzip header, so the size cannot tell.
    try:
        old = pd.read_csv(path)
    except pd.errors.EmptyDataError:
        return new
    # A run of no model replaces nothing.
    if new.empty:
        return old
    if "model" not in old or "model" not in new:
        return new
    kept = old.loc[~old["model"].isin(set(new["model"]))]
    if kept.empty:
        return new
    return pd.concat([kept, new], ignore_index=True)

def score_tasks(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    truth: pd.DataFrame,
    truth_date: str,
    complete_after_weeks: int = 0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score forecasts on every week against one truth vintage.

    Forecasts made at or after `truth_date` are dropped.
    Every week the truth covers is scored, as reported at `truth_date`.
    Final-count rows (no `as_of`) are scored `"as reported"`.
    Rows with `as_of` equal to `truth_date` predict the counts as reported
    then, and are scored `"vintage-matched"`. Rows for other dates are
    left out.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `run_forecasts`.
    truth : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `truth`.
    truth_date : str
        The date of the truth data.
    complete_after_weeks : int
        $K$: weeks that ended at least this many weeks before `truth_date`
        are flagged `complete`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `nowcasteval.scoring.score_forecasts`, with
        `truth_vintage`, `scoring` and `complete` columns.
    """
    keep = forecasts["vintage"] < truth_date
    as_of = (
        forecasts["as_of"]
        if "as_of" in forecasts
        else pd.Series(np.nan, index=forecasts.index)
    )
    frames = []
    for scoring, rows in (
        ("as reported", as_of.isna()),
        ("vintage-matched", as_of == truth_date),
    ):
        sel = forecasts.loc[keep & rows].drop(columns="as_of", errors="ignore")
        if sel.empty:
            continue
        scores = score_forecasts(sel, truth)
        scores["scoring"] = scoring
        frames.append(scores)
    if not frames:
        return pd.DataFrame()
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    out["truth_vintage"] = truth_date
    age = pd.Timestamp(truth_date) - pd.to_datetime(out["target_end_date"])
    out["complete"] = age.dt.days >= 7 * complete_after_weeks
    return out

    )
    out["truth_vintage"] = truth_date

def truth_changes(
    target: pd.DataFrame, locations: Sequence[str] | None = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Show each week's truth in every real vintage and its change since.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows with every real vintage.
    locations : sequence of str, optional
        Locations to keep. All if None.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `truth_vintage`, `truth`
        and `change`, this vintage's value minus the latest one. A
        negative change means the week has been revised upwards since.
        Sorted by location, week and vintage.
    """
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    if locations is not None:
        real = real.loc[real["location"].isin(list(locations))]
    out = real[["location", "target_end_date", "vintage", "total"]].rename(
        columns={"vintage": "truth_vintage", "total": "truth"}
    )
    latest = out.loc[out["truth_vintage"] == out["truth_vintage"].max()]
    out = out.merge(
        latest[["location", "target_end_date", "truth"]],
        on=["location", "target_end_date"],
        suffixes=("", "_latest"),
    )
    out["change"] = out["truth"] - out.pop("truth_latest")
    return out.sort_values(
        ["location", "target_end_date", "truth_vintage"]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

def joint_order(forecasts: pd.DataFrame, models: Sequence[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Put forecasts stacked by model in the order one run makes them.

    `run_forecasts` runs every model on a task before the next task. Rows
    are sorted by vintage, then by model in the order of `models`, and
    otherwise kept in order.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        Forecasts with `vintage` and `model`.
    models : sequence of str
        The models in the order one run takes them.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The rows reordered, with a fresh index.
    """
    if forecasts.empty:
        return forecasts.reset_index(drop=True)
    rank = forecasts["model"].map({m: i for i, m in enumerate(models)})
    order = np.lexsort((rank.to_numpy(), forecasts["vintage"].astype(str)))
    return forecasts.iloc[order].reset_index(drop=True)

docs.text:
Backtest of every model on the real releases.

Every real release with a later release is an origin. The random walk models forecast from the releases up to the origin only (nowcastbaselines.randomwalk). Stored forecasts of other models, such as the renewal models and hub teams, are scored with them. Weeks back $k$ count from the week holding the origin's cut-off, so forecast weeks have $k < 0$. Two targets are scored.

Reported. The count each later release $o'$ shows, for every week of the forecast that $o'$ reports. randomwalk is scored on its samples as they are, with no delay. Every other model forecasts the final count $X$ of a week and is mapped to what $o'$ shows through its own modelled delay, the share $\pi$ of a day's final count reported by each age (delay_curves, week_shares). Of the count $X - R_o$ outstanding at the origin, with $R_o$ the count reported there, $o'$ reports a draw from $\text{Binomial}(X - R_o, q)$, with $q = (\pi_{o'} - \pi_o) / (1 - \pi_o)$ (draw_reported). A model with no modelled delay, such as a hub team, is scored on complete weeks only.

Complete weeks. The count the latest release shows for the weeks it reports in full, decided from the releases alone and never from a model (complete_weeks). By default a week is complete when it is at least COMPLETE_WEEKS weeks old at the latest release and grew by less than COMPLETE_GROWTH between the last two releases. With a truth delay $D$, each week's truth is instead its count in the first release whose cut-off is at least $D$ days after the week ends (rolling_truth), and weeks no release has reached yet are not scored. The backtest takes $D$ from its config, or estimates it as the age by which TRUTH_LEVEL of the national count is reported (reporting_delay, resolve_truth_delay).

A model that cannot forecast from an origin, such as a nowcast with no pair of releases within the delay window, is listed with no forecasts there. A model with no snapshots stops the run.

Scores are CRPS, log CRPS, coverage and bias (nowcasteval.scoring) and every table counts its forecasts, $n$. The energy score is scored from the same drawn samples, one per origin, release, target and scale.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ForecastParts:
    """Tables of a forecast run, written one file each and stacked by `read`.

    A subclass lists its tables, in field order, in `_NAMES` and names
    their files with `_FILE`, a format string taking the table's name.
    """

    _NAMES: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ()
    _FILE: ClassVar[str] = "{}.csv.gz"

    def write(self, out: Path | str) -> None:
        """Write each table to `out`, as named by `_FILE`."""
        Path(out).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for name in self._NAMES:
            write_csv(getattr(self, name), Path(out) / self._FILE.format(name))

    @classmethod
    def read(cls, parts: Sequence[Path | str]) -> Self:
        """Stack the tables `write` wrote to each part, in order."""
        tables = {}
        for name in cls._NAMES:
            frames = []
            for part in parts:
                try:
                    frame = pd.read_csv(
                        Path(part) / cls._FILE.format(name),
                        dtype={"origin": str, "vintage": str},
                        keep_default_na=False,
                        na_values=[""],
                    )
                except pd.errors.EmptyDataError:
                    continue
                frames.append(frame)
            # A part with no rows (a block every model skips) adds none.
            frames = [f for f in frames if len(f)] or frames[:1]
            tables[name] = stack_parts(frames)
        return cls(**tables)

@classmethod
def read(cls, parts: Sequence[Path | str]) -> Self:
    """Stack the tables `write` wrote to each part, in order."""
    tables = {}
    for name in cls._NAMES:
        frames = []
        for part in parts:
            try:
                frame = pd.read_csv(
                    Path(part) / cls._FILE.format(name),
                    dtype={"origin": str, "vintage": str},
                    keep_default_na=False,
                    na_values=[""],
                )
            except pd.errors.EmptyDataError:
                continue
            frames.append(frame)
        # A part with no rows (a block every model skips) adds none.
        frames = [f for f in frames if len(f)] or frames[:1]
        tables[name] = stack_parts(frames)
    return cls(**tables)

def delay_curves(summary: pd.DataFrame, places: Sequence[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return a model's share of a day's final count reported by age.

    Each place takes the model's delay at that place, and a zone with none
    its province's. A place with neither, such as a province never seeded,
    takes the model's common delay: its shared delay (location `"shared"`),
    as in the renewal model, or the pooled delay (`"pooled"`) that fits
    from before province delays store for every place. The country takes
    none and is the sum of its provinces.

    Parameters
    ----------
    summary : pandas.DataFrame
        The model's delay summary (`delay_summary`), with `location`,
        `x` (age in days), `quantity` and `q50`. The rows with quantity
        `reported_share` are used.
    places : sequence of str
        The places to map.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `age` and `share`, for the places the model
        has a delay for.
    """
    rows = summary.loc[summary["quantity"] == "reported_share"]
    rows = rows.rename(columns={"x": "age", "q50": "share"})
    by_place = {str(loc): grp for loc, grp in rows.groupby("location")}
    common = next((k for k in ("pooled", "shared") if k in by_place), None)
    frames = []
    for place in places:
        if place in by_place:
            key = place
        elif province_of(place) in by_place:
            key = province_of(place)
        elif place != NATIONAL and common is not None:
            key = common
        else:
            continue
        frames.append(by_place[key].assign(location=place))
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True) if frames else rows.iloc[:0]
    return out.astype({"age": int})[["location", "age", "share"]]

def week_shares(
    curves: pd.DataFrame, cutoff: dt.date, weeks: Sequence[str]
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    r"""Return the share of each week's final count reported by a cut-off.

    Day $t$ is $a = c - t$ days old at cut-off $c$, with share $\pi(a)$
    from the place's curve, its last value past the curve's ages, and
    $\pi = 0$ for days after the cut-off.
    A week's share is the mean over its seven days.

    Parameters
    ----------
    curves : pandas.DataFrame
        `delay_curves` output.
    cutoff : datetime.date
        The cut-off of the release.
    weeks : sequence of str
        Hub week ends.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `share`, for every
        place in `curves`.
    """
    ends = [as_date(w) for w in weeks]
    age = np.array([[(cutoff - e).days + d for d in range(7)] for e in ends])
    frames = []
    for loc, grp in curves.groupby("location"):
        c = grp.sort_values("age")
        pi = np.where(
            age >= 0,
            np.interp(age, c["age"].to_numpy(), c["share"].to_numpy()),
            0.0,
        )
        frames.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "target_end_date": list(weeks),
                    "share": pi.mean(axis=1),
                }
            )
        )
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)

def draw_reported(
    samples: pd.DataFrame,
    reported: pd.DataFrame,
    now: pd.DataFrame,
    then: pd.DataFrame,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    r"""Draw the count a later release reports from samples of the final count.

    Of the count $X - R_o$ outstanding at the origin, with $R_o$ the count
    reported there, the later release $o'$ reports a binomial draw with
    probability $q = (\pi_{o'} - \pi_o) / (1 - \pi_o)$, the share it is
    expected to report. Each sample becomes
    $R_o + \text{Binomial}(X - R_o, q)$, with the sign carried when
    $X < R_o$. A week fully reported at the origin has $q = 1$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample` and `value`.
    reported : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `reported`, the counts
        at the origin. Weeks not in it have 0 reported.
    now, then : pandas.DataFrame
        `week_shares` at the origin's cut-off and the later one's.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator
        Random numbers.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The samples of the places and weeks in `now`, drawn.
    """
    keys = ["location", "target_end_date"]
    share = now.merge(then, on=keys, suffixes=("_o", "_l"))
    rows = samples.merge(share, on=keys).merge(reported, on=keys, how="left")
    pi_o, pi_l = rows.pop("share_o"), rows.pop("share_l")
    q = np.divide(
        pi_l - pi_o, 1.0 - pi_o, out=np.ones(len(rows)), where=pi_o < 1.0
    ).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    r = rows.pop("reported").fillna(0.0)
    left = np.round(rows["value"] - r).astype(np.int64)
    rows["value"] = r + np.sign(left) * rng.binomial(np.abs(left), q)
    return rows

def complete_weeks(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    daily: pd.DataFrame,
    vintage: str,
    rule: str = "growth",
    weeks: int = COMPLETE_WEEKS,
    growth: float = COMPLETE_GROWTH,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Say which weeks a release reports in full, from the releases alone.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy target table, with every real release.
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Daily onsets by release, for the release's cut-off.
    vintage : str
        The release.
    rule : str
        `"growth"`: at least `weeks` old and grew by less than `growth`
        since the release before. `"age"`: at least `weeks` old.
    weeks : int
        Weeks back from the week holding the release's cut-off.
    growth : float
        Most a complete week may grow, as a share of its earlier count.
        A week at 0 in both releases has grown by 0.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `age` (weeks back),
        `growth` and `complete`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `rule` is not `"growth"` or `"age"`.
    """
    if rule not in ("growth", "age"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown rule {rule!r}: use 'growth' or 'age'.")
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    releases = sorted(str(v) for v in real["vintage"].unique())
    before = [v for v in releases if v < vintage]
    rows = truth_from_vintage(real, vintage).rename(columns={"truth": "now"})
    if before:
        prev = truth_from_vintage(real, before[-1]).rename(
            columns={"truth": "then"}
        )
        rows = rows.merge(prev, on=["location", "target_end_date"], how="left")
    else:
        rows["then"] = np.nan
    up = rows["now"] - rows["then"]
    rows["growth"] = np.where(
        rows["then"] > 0,
        up / rows["then"].where(rows["then"] > 0, 1.0),
        np.where(up > 0, np.inf, 0.0),
    )
    rows.loc[rows["then"].isna(), "growth"] = np.nan
    rows["age"] = weeks_back_from_cutoff(
        daily, vintage, rows["target_end_date"]
    )
    old = rows["age"] >= weeks
    if rule == "growth":
        old &= rows["growth"].fillna(np.inf) < growth
    rows["complete"] = old
    return rows[
        ["location", "target_end_date", "age", "growth", "complete"]
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

def reported_samples(
    samples: pd.DataFrame,
    summary: pd.DataFrame | None,
    model: str,
    origin: str,
    later: Sequence[str],
    daily: pd.DataFrame,
    reported: pd.DataFrame,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return a model's samples of what each later release shows.

    `randomwalk`'s samples are returned as they are, with no delay.
    Another model's places are mapped by its delay (`delay_curves`,
    `draw_reported`), a place it has no delay for is returned as it is,
    and the country is the sum of the provinces.
    A model with no delay summary, such as a hub team, has none.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        The model's final-count samples, with `location`,
        `target_end_date`, `sample` and `value`.
    summary : pandas.DataFrame or None
        The model's delay summary at the origin.
    model : str
        The model's name.
    origin : str
        The origin release.
    later : sequence of str
        The later releases.
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Daily onsets by release, for the cut-offs.
    reported : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `reported`, the counts
        at the origin.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator
        Random numbers.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to pandas.DataFrame
        Samples by later release.
    """
    if model == RANDOM_WALK:
        return dict.fromkeys(later, samples)
    if summary is None:
        return {}
    places = samples.loc[samples["location"] != NATIONAL]
    curves = delay_curves(summary, sorted(set(places["location"])))
    mapped = places["location"].isin(set(curves["location"]))
    whole = NATIONAL in set(samples["location"])
    if not mapped.any():
        kept = add_national(places) if whole else places
        return dict.fromkeys(later, kept)
    weeks = sorted(set(samples["target_end_date"]))
    now = week_shares(curves, release_cutoff(daily, origin), weeks)
    out = {}
    for o2 in later:
        then = week_shares(curves, release_cutoff(daily, o2), weeks)
        drawn = draw_reported(places.loc[mapped], reported, now, then, rng)
        both = pd.concat([drawn, places.loc[~mapped]], ignore_index=True)
        out[o2] = add_national(both) if whole else both
    return out

def rolling_truth(target: pd.DataFrame, delay: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each week's count in the first release `delay` days after it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows of every release, with `vintage`, `cutoff`,
        `location`, `target_end_date` and `total`.
    delay : int
        $D$, the days from the end of a week to the cut-off of the release
        that gives its truth.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `truth` and
        `truth_vintage`, the release used. Weeks with no release $D$ days
        after them have no row.
    """
    due = pd.to_datetime(target["target_end_date"]) + pd.Timedelta(days=delay)
    late = target.loc[pd.to_datetime(target["cutoff"]) >= due]
    first = late.sort_values(["cutoff", "vintage"]).drop_duplicates(
        ["location", "target_end_date"]
    )
    out = first.rename(columns={"total": "truth", "vintage": "truth_vintage"})
    return out[
        ["location", "target_end_date", "truth", "truth_vintage"]
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

def reporting_delay(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    level: float = TRUTH_LEVEL,
    skip: Collection[str] = (),
    location: str = NATIONAL,
) -> int | None:
    """Return the age in days by which `level` of a place's count is reported.

    Each earlier release's count of a week is set against the latest
    release's count of that week, at the week's age in the release: the
    days from the week's end to the release, rounded up to whole weeks.
    The counts are pooled over releases at each age.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows of every release, with `vintage`, `location`,
        `target_end_date` and `total`.
    level : float
        The share of the latest count to reach.
    skip : collection of str
        Releases left out, as revisions rather than reporting delays.
    location : str
        The place, by default the country.

    Returns
    -------
    int or None
        The first age, in days, whose pooled share reaches `level`, or
        None if none does.
    """
    rows = target.loc[target["location"] == location]
    vintages = pd.to_datetime(rows["vintage"])
    weeks = pd.to_datetime(rows["target_end_date"])
    last = vintages == vintages.max()
    final = pd.Series(rows.loc[last, "total"].to_numpy(), weeks.loc[last])
    early = ~last & ~rows["vintage"].astype(str).isin(skip)
    days = (vintages - weeks).dt.days.loc[early]
    pooled = (
        pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "age": np.ceil(days / 7).astype(int),
                "reported": rows.loc[early, "total"],
                "final": weeks.loc[early].map(final),
            }
        )
        .dropna(subset=["final"])
        .groupby("age")[["reported", "final"]]
        .sum()
    )
    share = pooled["reported"] / pooled["final"].where(pooled["final"] > 0)
    reached = share.index[share >= level]
    return int(reached.min()) * 7 if len(reached) else None

def truth_sensitivity(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    daily: pd.DataFrame,
    levels: Sequence[float] = (0.9, 0.95, 0.98, 0.99),
    weeks: Sequence[int] = (3, 4, 5, 6),
    growths: Sequence[float] = (0.01, 0.02, 0.05),
    skip: Collection[str] = (),
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return how the truth-final constants move what is scored.

    Two checks on the releases alone, with no model:

    - `delays`: the truth delay $D$ (`reporting_delay`) at each `level`,
      the share of the national count reported by that age; missing
      where no age reaches it.
    - `complete`: for each `weeks` and `growth` of the `"growth"` rule
      (`complete_weeks`), the weeks each earlier release calls complete
      against the latest release: the share of place-weeks called
      complete (`complete`) and, of those, the share whose latest count
      differs from that release's by more than 2% (`revised_2pct`) and
      10% (`revised_10pct`) of the latest. `releases` is how many
      releases were checked (every one before the latest).

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy target table, with every real release.
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Daily onsets by release.
    levels : sequence of float
        Shares of the national count, each in (0, 1].
    weeks, growths : sequence
        The rule's ages and growth limits checked.
    skip : collection of str
        Releases left out of the delay, as `reporting_delay` takes them.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to pandas.DataFrame
        `delays` (`level`, `truth_delay`) and `complete` (`weeks`,
        `growth`, `releases`, `complete`, `revised_2pct`,
        `revised_10pct`).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a level is not above 0.
    """
    if any(lv <= 0 for lv in levels):
        raise ValueError(f"Each level must be above 0: {list(levels)}.")
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    delays = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "level": list(levels),
            "truth_delay": [
                reporting_delay(real, lv, skip) if lv <= 1 else None
                for lv in levels
            ],
        }
    )
    delays["truth_delay"] = delays["truth_delay"].astype("Float64")
    releases = sorted(real["vintage"].astype(str).unique())
    keys = ["location", "target_end_date"]

    def counts(v: str) -> pd.Series:
        rows = real.loc[real["vintage"].astype(str) == v]
        return rows.assign(
            target_end_date=rows["target_end_date"].astype(str)
        ).set_index(keys)["total"]

    latest = counts(releases[-1])
    out = []
    for w in weeks:
        for g in growths:
            called = 0
            seen = 0
            change: list[float] = []
            for v in releases[:-1]:
                done = complete_weeks(target, daily, v, "growth", w, g)
                done = done.assign(
                    target_end_date=done["target_end_date"].astype(str)
                )
                seen += len(done)
                idx = done.loc[done["complete"]].set_index(keys).index
                now = counts(v)
                idx = idx.intersection(now.index).intersection(latest.index)
                called += len(idx)
                diff = (latest.loc[idx] - now.loc[idx]).abs()
                change += list(diff / latest.loc[idx].clip(lower=1))
            rev = np.asarray(change, dtype=float)
            out.append(
                {
                    "weeks": w,
                    "growth": g,
                    "releases": len(releases) - 1,
                    "complete": called / seen if seen else np.nan,
                    "revised_2pct": float(np.mean(rev > 0.02))
                    if rev.size
                    else np.nan,
                    "revised_10pct": float(np.mean(rev > 0.1))
                    if rev.size
                    else np.nan,
                }
            )
    return {"delays": delays, "complete": pd.DataFrame(out)}

def resolve_truth_delay(config: BacktestConfig, target: pd.DataFrame) -> int:
    """Return the backtest's truth delay $D$, in days.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : BacktestConfig
        Gives a fixed `truth_delay`, or `truth_level` to estimate it with
        (`reporting_delay`), less a cumulative first release under
        `max_delay` (`truth_skip`).
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy target table.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        The fixed delay, or the estimated one.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the national count never reaches `truth_level`.
    """
    if config.truth_delay is not None:
        return config.truth_delay
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    delay = reporting_delay(real, config.truth_level, truth_skip(real, config))
    if delay is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No age has {config.truth_level:.0%} of the national count "
            "reported: set truth_delay, or a lower truth_level, in the "
            "backtest config."
        )
    return delay

def forecast_releases(
    tasks: Sequence[ForecastTask],
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    models: Sequence[str | ForecastModel] = ("randomwalk", "randomwalknowcast"),
) -> ReleaseForecasts:
    """Forecast from every real release with a later one, without scoring.

    The forecasting half of `release_backtest`: `score_releases` scores
    the result, alone or stacked with other models' (`ReleaseForecasts`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    tasks : sequence of ForecastTask
        One real task per release, with its release snapshots.
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy target table, for the releases.
    models : sequence of str or ForecastModel
        Registered model names, or models, to run.

    Returns
    -------
    ReleaseForecasts
        The forecasts, delay summaries and fit summaries.

    Raises
    ------
    MissingSnapshots
        If a task has no release snapshots.
    """
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    releases = sorted(str(v) for v in real["vintage"].unique())
    built = [get_model(m) if isinstance(m, str) else m for m in models]
    runs: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    samples, delays, fit_rows = [], [], []
    for task in sorted(tasks, key=lambda t: t.vintage):
        later = [v for v in releases if v > task.vintage]
        if task.kind != "real" or not later:
            continue
        if task.daily_history is None or task.daily_history.empty:
            raise MissingSnapshots(
                f"Release backtest needs daily release snapshots, and the "
                f"task for {task.vintage} has none."
            )
        for model in built:
            try:
                drawn = model.forecast(task)
            except ModelUnavailableError as err:
                log.warning("%s has no forecast at %s: %s", model.name,
                            task.vintage, err)  # fmt: skip
                runs.append(
                    {
                        "origin": task.vintage,
                        "model": model.name,
                        "status": "no forecast",
                        "reason": str(err),
                    }
                )
                continue
            runs.append(
                {
                    "origin": task.vintage,
                    "model": model.name,
                    "status": "forecast",
                    "reason": "",
                }
            )
            samples.append(
                add_national(drawn).assign(
                    model=model.name, origin=task.vintage
                )
            )
            summary = getattr(model, "delay_summary", None)
            if summary is not None:
                delays.append(summary.assign(origin=task.vintage))
            fits = pd.DataFrame(getattr(model, "fit_diagnostics", []))
            fits.insert(0, "model", model.name)
            fits.insert(1, "origin", task.vintage)
            fit_rows.append(fits)

    return ReleaseForecasts(
        pd.DataFrame(runs, columns=["origin", "model", "status", "reason"]),
        stack_parts(samples),
        stack_parts(delays),
        stack_parts(fit_rows),
    )

def score_releases(
    tasks: Sequence[ForecastTask],
    daily: pd.DataFrame,
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    run: ReleaseForecasts,
    stored: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    delays: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    complete_rule: str = "growth",
    complete_after: int = COMPLETE_WEEKS,
    compare: Collection[str] | None = None,
    truth_delay: int | None = None,
) -> ReleaseBacktest:
    """Score the forecasts of `forecast_releases` and of stored models.

    The scoring half of `release_backtest`, which it equals given the
    same tasks and models. Models are taken at each origin in the order
    they were run, then the stored models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tasks : sequence of ForecastTask
        As for `release_backtest`.
    daily, target : pandas.DataFrame
        As for `release_backtest`.
    run : ReleaseForecasts
        The run models' forecasts.
    stored, delays : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        As for `release_backtest`.
    complete_rule, complete_after : str, int
        As for `release_backtest`.
    compare : collection of str, optional
        As for `release_backtest`.
    truth_delay : int, optional
        As for `release_backtest`.

    Returns
    -------
    ReleaseBacktest
        As `release_backtest`.
    """
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    releases = sorted(str(v) for v in real["vintage"].unique())
    latest = releases[-1]
    cols = ["location", "target_end_date", "sample", "value"]
    kept = pd.DataFrame(columns=["model", "vintage", *cols])
    kept = kept if stored is None else stored
    runs = run.runs.astype({"origin": str})
    samples = (
        run.samples.astype({"origin": str})
        if len(run.samples)
        else (run.samples)
    )
    frames: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    origin_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    fit_rows: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for task in sorted(tasks, key=lambda t: t.vintage):
        later = [v for v in releases if v > task.vintage]
        if task.kind != "real" or not later:
            continue
        here = kept.loc[kept["vintage"].astype(str) == task.vintage]
        forecasts: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
        summaries: dict[str, pd.DataFrame | None] = {}
        for row in runs.loc[runs["origin"] == task.vintage].itertuples():
            name: str = str(row.model)
            if row.status == "no forecast":
                origin_rows.append(
                    {
                        "origin": task.vintage,
                        "model": name,
                        "status": "no forecast",
                        "reason": str(row.reason),
                    }
                )
                continue
            mine = (samples["model"] == name) & (
                samples["origin"] == task.vintage
            )
            forecasts[name] = (
                samples.loc[mine]
                .drop(columns=["model", "origin"])
                .reset_index(drop=True)
            )
            summaries[name] = model_origin_rows(run.delays, name, task.vintage)
            fit_rows.append(_fit_part(run.fits, name, task.vintage))
        _check_distinct(forecasts, task.vintage)
        learnt = (
            pd.DataFrame(columns=["model", "vintage"])
            if delays is None
            else delays.loc[delays["vintage"].astype(str) == task.vintage]
        )
        for key, grp in here.groupby("model"):
            forecasts[str(key)] = grp[cols]
            have = learnt.loc[learnt["model"] == key]
            summaries[str(key)] = None if have.empty else have
        reported = truth_from_vintage(real, task.vintage).rename(
            columns={"truth": "reported"}
        )
        # Each model draws from its own stream, so its scores do not depend
        # on which other models run.
        rngs = {name: task.rng(name) for name in forecasts}
        for name, drawn in forecasts.items():
            frames += [
                _label(by, name, task.vintage, "reported", o2, daily)
                for o2, by in reported_samples(
                    drawn, summaries[name], name, task.vintage, later,
                    daily, reported, rngs[name],
                ).items()
            ]  # fmt: skip
            frames.append(
                _label(drawn, name, task.vintage, "complete", latest, daily)
            )
        origin_rows += [
            {
                "origin": task.vintage,
                "model": name,
                "status": "scored",
                "reason": "",
            }
            for name in forecasts
        ]
    done = complete_weeks(
        target, daily, latest, rule=complete_rule, weeks=complete_after
    )
    complete = (
        truth_from_vintage(real, latest)
        .assign(truth_vintage=latest)
        .merge(
            done.loc[done["complete"], ["location", "target_end_date"]],
            on=["location", "target_end_date"],
        )
        if truth_delay is None
        else rolling_truth(real, truth_delay)
    )
    if truth_delay is not None:
        # Each complete week is labelled with the release giving its truth,
        # and weeks with none yet are dropped, quantiles included.
        frames = [_relabel(f, complete) for f in frames]
    return _score(frames, origin_rows, fit_rows, real, done, complete, compare)

def model_origin_rows(
    table: pd.DataFrame, model: str, origin: str
) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    """Return a run model's rows at an origin, without `origin`, or None.

    Parameters
    ----------
    table : pandas.DataFrame

        The model.

        The origin, compared as text.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame or None
        None if the table or the model's rows at the origin are empty.

    if table.empty or "origin" not in table:
        return None
    mine = table.loc[
        (table["model"] == model) & (table["origin"].astype(str) == origin)
    ]
    if mine.empty:
        return None
    return mine.drop(columns="origin").reset_index(drop=True)

        90% intervals and bias.

    cols = ["crps", "coverage_50", "coverage_90", "bias"]
    assert set(cols) <= set(SCORE_COLUMNS)

    out = grp[cols].mean()
    out.insert(0, "n", grp.size())
    return out.reset_index()

def relative_crps(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    by: Sequence[str] = ("target",),
    baseline: str = "randomwalk",
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return each model's pairwise relative CRPS and its own mean scores.

    The relative CRPS and log CRPS are `nowcasteval.scoring.pairwise_skill`
    scaled to the baseline, so models that forecast different cells (a
    stored model that missed origins) compare fairly. The means are over
    each model's own forecasts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        `ReleaseBacktest.scores`.
    by : sequence of str
        Columns of a cell other than `model`.
    baseline : str
        The model the relative scores are scaled to.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per cell and model: `n` (its forecasts), `crps`,
        `base_crps` (the baseline's mean CRPS in the cell), `rel_crps`,
        `rel_log_crps` (pairwise; missing for a model that shares no
        forecast with any other), the coverage of the 50% and 90%
        intervals and the mean `bias`.
    """
    by = list(by)
    match = ("target", "origin", "truth_vintage", "location", "target_end_date")
    rel = pairwise_skill(
        scores,
        baseline,
        by=by,
        metrics=("crps", "log_crps"),
        match_on=match,
        rounds="origin",
    )
    cols = ["crps", "coverage_50", "coverage_90", "bias"]
    means = scores.groupby([*by, "model"])[cols].mean().reset_index()
    base = means.loc[means["model"] == baseline, [*by, "crps"]]
    base = base.rename(columns={"crps": "base_crps"})
    out = rel.merge(means, on=[*by, "model"])
    out = (
        (
            out.merge(base, on=by, how="left")
            if by
            else out.assign(
                base_crps=base["base_crps"].iloc[0] if len(base) else np.nan
            )
        )
        .rename(
            columns={
                "relative_crps": "rel_crps",
                "relative_log_crps": "rel_log_crps",
            }
        )
        .sort_values([*by, "model"])
    )
    order = [
        "n",
        "crps",
        "base_crps",
        "rel_crps",
        "rel_log_crps",
        "coverage_50",
        "coverage_90",
        "bias",
    ]
    return out[[*by, "model", *order]].reset_index(drop=True)

def forecast_quantiles(
    model: ForecastModel,
    task: ForecastTask,
    levels: Sequence[float],
    n_draws: int = N_DRAWS,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return one model's forecasts of one task as quantiles at `levels`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : ForecastModel
        The model. Its own quantiles are used where it gives them.
    task : ForecastTask
        The task. Its `n_samples` and `seed` are replaced.
    levels : sequence of float
        Increasing quantile levels.
    n_draws : int
        Draws where the quantiles come from draws.
    seed : int
        The task's seed for those draws, the same for every model.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `run_forecasts` columns with `sample` replaced by `quantile`: one
        row per location, week and level, the country included.
    """
    at = np.asarray(levels, dtype=float)
    own = _own_quantiles(model, task, at)
    if own is not None:
        return own
    if hasattr(model, "stream"):
        model = _with_stream(model)
    drawn = run_forecasts(
        [model], [dataclasses.replace(task, n_samples=n_draws, seed=seed)]
    )
    keys = [c for c in drawn.columns if c not in ("sample", "value")]
    return (
        drawn.groupby(keys, dropna=False)["value"]
        .quantile(at)
        .rename_axis([*keys, "quantile"])
        .reset_index()
    )

def summarise_draws(
    observed: pd.DataFrame,
    draws: ArrayLike,
    *,
    as_of: str | dt.date,
    model: str = "renewal",
    config: str = "main",
    complete_lag_weeks: int = 4,
    intervals: Sequence[float] = (0.5, 0.9),
    seed: int = 1,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarise posterior predictive draws against the observed counts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    observed : pandas.DataFrame
        One row per location, stream and onset week, with columns
        `location`, `stream` (one of `STREAMS`), `target_end_date`
        (ISO date) and `observed` (the count in the data vintage).
    draws : array_like
        Posterior predictive draws of the observed counts, of shape
        `(n_draws, len(observed))`, with column `j` matching row `j` of
        `observed`.
    as_of : str or datetime.date
        Data vintage. Weeks ending at least `complete_lag_weeks` weeks
        before it are marked complete.
    model, config : str
        Model and configuration, recorded in the payload.
    complete_lag_weeks : int
        Completeness lag in weeks.
    intervals : sequence of float
        Central interval levels, such as `(0.5, 0.9)`. Each adds
        `lower_<pct>` and `upper_<pct>` to the rows.
    seed : int
        Seed of the uniform draws in the randomised PIT, so the payload
        is reproducible.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The `ppc.json` payload, with `available` true.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a column is missing, a stream is unknown, or the draws do
        not match the rows.

    Notes
    -----
    The PIT is the randomised PIT for counts:
    `F(y - 1) + v * (F(y) - F(y - 1))` with `v ~ Uniform(0, 1)` and `F`
    the empirical predictive distribution function, using `P(X < y)` for
    `F(y - 1)`. It is uniform on (0, 1) under a calibrated model, even
    though the counts are discrete.
    """
    missing = [c for c in _COLUMNS if c not in observed.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"observed lacks columns {missing}")
    unknown = sorted(set(observed["stream"]) - set(STREAMS))
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown streams {unknown}; use {list(STREAMS)}")
    x = np.asarray(draws, dtype=float)
    if x.ndim != 2 or x.shape[1] != len(observed):
        raise ValueError(
            f"draws have shape {x.shape}, not (n_draws, {len(observed)})"
        )
    levels = [float(level) for level in intervals]
    if not all(0 < level < 1 for level in levels):
        raise ValueError(f"interval levels must be in (0, 1): {levels}")
    y = observed["observed"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    below = (x < y).mean(axis=0)
    at_or_below = (x <= y).mean(axis=0)
    v = np.random.default_rng(seed).uniform(size=len(y))
    pit = below + v * (at_or_below - below)
    probs = [0.5]
    for level in levels:
        probs += [(1 - level) / 2, (1 + level) / 2]
    q = np.quantile(x, probs, axis=0) if len(y) else np.empty((len(probs), 0))
    vintage = dt.date.fromisoformat(str(as_of))
    cutoff = (vintage - dt.timedelta(weeks=complete_lag_weeks)).isoformat()
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    weeks = pd.to_datetime(observed["target_end_date"]).dt.date.astype(str)
    columns = zip(
        observed["location"].astype(str),
        observed["stream"].astype(str),
        weeks,
        y,
        strict=True,
    )
    for j, (location, stream, week, obs) in enumerate(columns):
        row: dict[str, Any] = {
            "location": location,
            "stream": stream,
            "target_end_date": week,
            "observed": int(obs) if float(obs).is_integer() else float(obs),
            "median": float(q[0, j]),
        }
        for k, level in enumerate(levels):
            row[f"lower_{_pct(level)}"] = float(q[1 + 2 * k, j])
            row[f"upper_{_pct(level)}"] = float(q[2 + 2 * k, j])
        row["pit"] = float(pit[j])
        row["complete"] = week <= cutoff
        rows.append(row)
    return {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "available": True,
        "model": model,
        "config": config,
        "intervals": levels,
        "rows": rows,
    }

    data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(data, dict):

    if data["available"] and not isinstance(data.get("rows"), list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no 'rows' list")
    return data
