def plot_ppc(
    ppc: Mapping[str, Any], stream: str = "total", ncol: int = 3
) -> Figure:
    """Plot the posterior predictive intervals against the observed counts.

    Small multiples by location, largest first, in light mode on a white
    background, for the submission gate's `ppc.png` artefact.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ppc : mapping
        A `ppc.json` payload with `available` true.
    stream : str
        Stream to show. Falls back to the first stream present.
    ncol : int
        Panels per row.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Per location: the predictive median with the widest and
        narrowest intervals, and the observed counts, hollow for
        incomplete weeks and marked where outside the widest interval.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the payload is not available or has no rows.
    """
    if not ppc.get("available"):
        raise ValueError(f"no posterior predictive checks: {ppc.get('reason')}")
    table = pd.DataFrame(ppc.get("rows") or [])
    if table.empty:
        raise ValueError("ppc.json has no rows")
    if stream not in set(table["stream"]):
        stream = str(table["stream"].iloc[0])
    table = table.loc[table["stream"] == stream].copy()
    table["date"] = pd.to_datetime(table["target_end_date"])
    sizes = table.groupby("location")["observed"].sum()
    locations = list(sizes.sort_values(ascending=False).index)
    pcts = sorted(_pct(level) for level in ppc.get("intervals", []))
    wide, narrow = (pcts[-1], pcts[0]) if pcts else (None, None)
    with theme("light") as ink:
        colour = model_colour("model", ["model"], "light")
        miss = model_colour("miss", ["model", "miss"], "light")
        fig, axes = panel_grid(len(locations), ncol, width=3.6, height=2.4)
        fig.set_facecolor("white")
        for ax, loc in zip(axes, locations, strict=True):
            d = table.loc[table["location"] == loc].sort_values("date")
            ax.set_facecolor("white")
            for pct, alpha in ((wide, 0.18), (narrow, 0.35)):
                if pct is None or f"lower_{pct}" not in d:
                    continue
                ax.fill_between(
                    d["date"],
                    d[f"lower_{pct}"],
                    d[f"upper_{pct}"],
                    color=colour,
                    alpha=alpha,
                    lw=0,
                    label=f"{pct}% interval",
                )
            ax.plot(
                d["date"], d["median"], color=colour, lw=1.2, label="Median"
            )
            done = d["complete"].astype(bool)
            out = np.zeros(len(d), dtype=bool)
            if wide is not None and f"lower_{wide}" in d:
                out = (
                    (d["observed"] < d[f"lower_{wide}"])
                    | (d["observed"] > d[f"upper_{wide}"])
                ).to_numpy()
            ax.scatter(
                d["date"][done],
                d["observed"][done],
                s=10,
                color=ink["data"],
                zorder=3,
                label="Observed (complete week)",
            )
            ax.scatter(
                d["date"][~done],
                d["observed"][~done],
                s=10,
                facecolors="white",
                edgecolors=ink["data"],
                zorder=3,
                label="Observed (incomplete week)",
            )
            ax.scatter(
                d["date"][out],
                d["observed"][out],
                s=28,
                facecolors="none",
                edgecolors=miss,
                lw=1.2,
                zorder=4,
                label=f"Outside the {wide}% interval",
            )
            cov = _coverage(d, wide) if wide is not None else float("nan")
            label = f", {wide}% coverage {cov:.2f}" if cov == cov else ""
            ax.set_title(f"{loc}{label}", fontsize=9)
            # matplotlib's date formatters are untyped.
            fmt = DateFormatter("%d %b")  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(fmt)
            ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=30)
        axes[0].set_ylabel("Cases by onset week")
        handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
        fig.legend(
            handles, labels, loc="outside lower center", ncol=3, fontsize=7
        )
        fig.suptitle(
            f"Posterior predictive check: {ppc.get('model', 'model')} "
            f"({ppc.get('config', '')}), {stream} onsets",
            color=ink["ink"],
            fontsize=10,
        )
    return fig

docs.text:
Plausibility checks of the backtest forecasts, scored.

Each forecast of a place from an origin $o$ gets a place type and a flag, both decided from the counts reported at $o$, and the scores of its scored weeks are then averaged by each. Week $w$ is the latest week ending on or before $o$, and $c(t)$ the count reported at $o$ for the week ending $t$, 0 where none is.

Place type. From the largest count $m$ of the recent weeks up to $w$ (the caller's window; the report uses the random walk's): silent if $m = 0$, small if $m \le$ SMALL_MAX, larger otherwise.

Flag. From the forecast of week $w + 1$, the first week after the origin's latest full week, with median $q_{50}$ and 95% quantile $q_{95}$. This is not always the round's reference week, which is $w + 2$ for an origin from Wednesday to Friday. The level is $\ell = \max{(c(w - 3) + c(w - 2)) / 2,\ c(w - 1)}$, the mean of the two latest weeks at least two weeks old, or the last full week's count where that is higher, as reported counts only grow. The recent maximum is $r = \max(1, \max_{w - 4 \le t \le w} c(t))$.

  • Collapse: $\ell \ge 3$ and $q_{50} \le \ell / 3$.
  • Blow-up: $q_{50} > 3r$ and $q_{50} - r \ge 5$, or $q_{95} > 10r$ and $q_{95} - r \ge 20$.

The thresholds pick out forecasts far from every recent count.

def flags(counts: pd.DataFrame, quantiles: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the flag of each forecast, from its week $w + 1$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    counts : pandas.DataFrame
        As for `place_types`.
    quantiles : pandas.DataFrame
        `model`, `origin`, `location`, `target_end_date`, `q50` and `q95`
        of each forecast's weeks.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model`, `origin`, `location` and `flag`, one of
        `collapse`, `blow-up` and `no flag`.
    """
    after = _last_week(quantiles["origin"]) + pd.Timedelta(days=7)
    quantiles = quantiles.loc[
        pd.to_datetime(quantiles["target_end_date"]) == after
    ]
    wide = _by_week(counts, quantiles, 5)
    level = pd.concat([(wide[3] + wide[2]) / 2, wide[1]], axis=1).max(axis=1)
    recent = wide[[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]].max(axis=1).clip(lower=1.0)
    out = quantiles.join(
        pd.DataFrame({"level": level, "recent": recent}),
        on=["origin", "location"],
    )
    q50, q95 = out["q50"], out["q95"]
    r, lv = out["recent"], out["level"]
    blow = ((q50 > 3 * r) & (q50 - r >= 5)) | ((q95 > 10 * r) & (q95 - r >= 20))
    collapse = (lv >= 3) & (q50 <= lv / 3)
    out["flag"] = "no flag"
    out.loc[blow, "flag"] = "blow-up"
    out.loc[collapse, "flag"] = "collapse"
    return out[["model", "origin", "location", "flag"]]

def check_summary(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    types: pd.DataFrame,
    flagged: pd.DataFrame,
    baseline: str,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Average the scores by scale, model and place type, and by flag.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        One row per scored week, `score_forecasts` output with `model`,
        `origin`, `location` and `scale`.
    types : pandas.DataFrame
        From `place_types`.
    flagged : pandas.DataFrame
        From `flags`.
    baseline : str
        The model relative CRPS divides by. Its CRPS is taken on the same
        scored weeks, whatever its own flag there. Relative CRPS is
        missing where the baseline's CRPS sums to 0.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `scale`, `split` (`place type` or `flag`), `group`,
        `model`, `n`, the mean of each metric and `relative CRPS`.
    """
    keyed = scores.merge(types, on=["origin", "location"], how="left").merge(
        flagged, on=["model", "origin", "location"], how="left"
    )
    week = ["origin", "truth_vintage", "location", "target_end_date"]
    base = scores.loc[scores["model"] == baseline, [*week, "crps"]]
    keyed = keyed.merge(
        base.rename(columns={"crps": "base_crps"}), on=week, how="left"
    )
    parts = []
    for split, col in (("place type", "place_type"), ("flag", "flag")):
        by = ["scale", col, "model"]
        sums = keyed.groupby(by)[["crps", "base_crps"]].sum()
        # A zero baseline gives no relative CRPS, as in `relative_skill`.
        base_sum = sums["base_crps"].where(sums["base_crps"] > 0)
        rel = (sums["crps"] / base_sum).rename("relative CRPS")
        parts.append(
            summarise_scores(keyed, by=by)
            .join(rel, on=by)
            .rename(columns={col: "group"})
            .assign(split=split)
        )
    out = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True).rename(columns=_METRICS)
    order = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(("place type", "flag", *_ORDER))}
    out = out.sort_values(
        ["scale", "split", "group", "model"],
        key=lambda c: c.map(order) if c.name in ("split", "group") else c,
    )
    cols = [
        "scale",
        "split",
        "group",
        "model",
        "n",
        "relative CRPS",
        *_METRICS.values(),
    ]
    return out[cols].reset_index(drop=True)

def variant_scores(
    samples: pd.DataFrame,
    truth: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    study: str,
    model: str,
    variant: str,
    origin: str,
    levels: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    national: str = NATIONAL,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score one variant of one forecast by level.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample` and `value`.
    truth : pandas.DataFrame
        `location`, `target_end_date` and `truth`. Only cells with a truth
        are scored.
    study, model, variant, origin : str
        Labels.
    levels : dict, optional
        A level for places that are neither the country nor zones (such as
        age groups); `provinces` by default.
    national : str
        The country's code.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `SCORE_COLUMNS`: the mean of each score over the forecast's cells
        or sums, and their number `n`.
    """
    rows = samples.merge(truth[[*_CELL, "truth"]], on=_CELL)
    if rows.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=list(SCORE_COLUMNS))
    rows = rows.assign(level=_level(rows["location"], levels or {}, national))
    found: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for level, grp in rows.groupby("level"):
        scored: list[dict[str, object]] = [
            *_sums(grp, _CELL, "cell"),
            *_sums(grp, ["location"], "sum_weeks"),
        ]
        if level == "zones":
            province = grp["location"].str.rsplit("-", n=1).str[0]
            scored += _sums(
                grp.assign(province=province),
                ["province", "target_end_date"],
                "sum_zones",
            )
            groups = list(grp.assign(province=province).groupby("province"))
        else:
            groups = [(level, grp)]
        for _, own in groups:
            wide = own.pivot(index="sample", columns=_CELL, values="value")
            obs = (
                own.drop_duplicates(_CELL)
                .set_index(_CELL)["truth"]
                .reindex(wide.columns)
                .to_numpy()
            )
            x = wide.to_numpy()
            scored += [
                {"target": "joint", "metric": "energy",
                 "value": energy_sample(obs, x)},
                {"target": "joint", "metric": "log_energy",
                 "value": energy_sample(np.log1p(obs), np.log1p(x))},
            ]  # fmt: skip
        frame = pd.DataFrame(scored)
        summary = frame.groupby(["target", "metric"], as_index=False).agg(
            value=("value", "mean"), n=("value", "size")
        )
        found.append(summary.assign(level=level))
    out = pd.concat(found, ignore_index=True).assign(
        study=study, model=model, variant=variant, origin=origin
    )
    return out[list(SCORE_COLUMNS)]

def summarise_pairing(scores: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the mean of each score by study, level, model and variant.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        `variant_scores` rows of many origins.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `study`, `level`, `model`, `variant`, `target`, `metric`, `value`
        (the mean over origins, weighted by each origin's `n`), `n` and
        `relative` (the value over the `off` variant's).
    """
    keys = ["study", "level", "model", "variant", "target", "metric"]
    weighted = scores.assign(total=scores["value"] * scores["n"])
    out = weighted.groupby(keys, as_index=False).agg(
        total=("total", "sum"), n=("n", "sum")
    )
    out["value"] = out["total"] / out["n"]
    base = out.loc[out["variant"] == "off"].set_index(
        [k for k in keys if k != "variant"]
    )["value"]
    idx = pd.MultiIndex.from_frame(out[[k for k in keys if k != "variant"]])
    out["relative"] = out["value"].to_numpy() / base.reindex(idx).to_numpy()
    return out[[*keys, "value", "n", "relative"]]

def best_candidate(scores: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rank the candidates by their mean provinces energy score.

    The energy score of each origin's provinces and weeks as one vector is
    the joint score the pairing is for. Each model's scores are divided by
    its own mean over candidates, so both models count alike.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        `bdbv_candidates`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per candidate (`variant`): `energy` (the mean relative
        energy score), `national_crps` (the same for the country, the sum
        of the provinces), and `fallback` (the share of origins that fell
        back to the prior), best first.
    """
    out = {}
    for metric, level, target in (
        ("energy", "provinces", "joint"),
        ("crps", "national", "cell"),
    ):
        rows = scores.loc[
            (scores["metric"] == metric)
            & (scores["level"] == level)
            & (scores["target"] == target)
        ]
        by = rows.groupby(["model", "variant", "origin"])["value"].mean()
        rel = by / by.groupby(["model", "origin"]).transform("mean")
        out[f"{'energy' if metric == 'energy' else 'national_crps'}"] = (
            rel.groupby("variant").mean()
        )
    table = pd.DataFrame(out)
    table["fallback"] = scores.groupby("variant")["fallback"].mean()
    return table.sort_values("energy").reset_index()

def model_label(model: str) -> str:
    """Return a model's display name.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : str
        A model id. A checkpoint `<id>@<outbreaks>` is named after its
        model with the outbreaks it was trained on, and `<id>_real` as
        fine-tuned on real data where `<id>`'s name has a variant in
        brackets. Ids without a name, such as hub teams, are returned
        unchanged.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The display name.
    """
    name, sep, size = model.rpartition(_CHECKPOINT)
    if sep and size.isdigit():
        return f"{model_label(name)}, {int(size):,} outbreaks"
    base = MODEL_LABELS.get(model.removesuffix(_REAL), "")
    if model.endswith(_REAL) and " (" in base:
        return f"Fine-tuned on real data ({base.split(' (', 1)[1]}"
    return MODEL_LABELS.get(model, model)

def model_colour(name: str, models: Sequence[str], mode: str = "light") -> str:
    """Return a model's fixed colour.

    A model in `MODEL_STYLE` has its own colour. Others, such as test
    stand-ins, take the colours after the last one `MODEL_STYLE` uses, in
    their order in `models`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The model.
    models : sequence of str
        All models shown.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        A hex colour.
    """
    palette = MODEL_COLOURS[mode]
    if name in MODEL_STYLE:
        return palette[MODEL_STYLE[name][0]]
    others = [m for m in models if m not in MODEL_STYLE]
    return palette[(_FREE_SLOT + others.index(name)) % len(palette)]

def save_light_dark(
    make: Callable[..., Figure], path: Path | str
) -> list[Path]:
    """Save a figure in light and dark versions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    make : callable
        Takes the keyword `mode` (`"light"` or `"dark"`) and returns a
        figure.
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        Output path for the light version, such as `figures/x.svg`. The
        dark version gets a `-dark` suffix.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The two paths written.
    """
    out = Path(path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths = [out, out.with_name(f"{out.stem}-dark{out.suffix}")]
    for mode, p in zip(("light", "dark"), paths, strict=True):
        with theme(mode):
            fig = make(mode=mode)
            fig.savefig(p, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close(fig)
    return paths

def panel_grid(
    n: int, ncol: int, width: float = 3.2, height: float = 2.4
) -> tuple[Figure, list[Axes]]:
    """Return a figure of `n` panels, `ncol` a row, and its used axes."""
    ncol = max(1, min(ncol, n))
    nrow = int(np.ceil(n / ncol))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        nrow,
        ncol,
        figsize=(width * ncol, height * nrow),
        squeeze=False,
        layout="constrained",
    )
    flat = list(axes.ravel())
    for ax in flat[n:]:
        ax.set_visible(False)
    return fig, flat[:n]

def plot_target(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    locations: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "light",  # noqa: ARG001 - shared signature
) -> Figure:
    """Plot weekly totals by onset week for each vintage, by location.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows of one kind.
    locations : sequence of str, optional
        Locations to show. Defaults to all with cases, largest first.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        One panel per location.
    """
    locs = list(locations or locations_by_size(target))
    vints = sorted(target["vintage"].unique())
    names = location_names(target)
    fig, axes = panel_grid(len(locs), 3)
    cmap = mpl.colormaps["Blues"]
    shades = np.linspace(0.35, 0.95, len(vints))
    for ax, loc in zip(axes, locs, strict=True):
        rows = target.loc[target["location"] == loc]
        for vin, shade in zip(vints, shades, strict=True):
            r = rows.loc[rows["vintage"] == vin]
            ax.plot(
                pd.to_datetime(r["target_end_date"]),
                r["total"],
                color=cmap(shade),
                lw=1.5,
                label=vin,
            )
        ax.set_title(f"{names.get(loc, loc)} ({loc})")
        date_axis(ax)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Confirmed cases by onset week")
    axes[0].legend(title="Vintage", title_fontsize=8)
    return fig

def plot_delay_distribution(
    delays: pd.DataFrame, max_delay: int = 40, mode: str = "light"
) -> Figure:
    """Plot the onset-to-report delay distribution by province.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delays : pandas.DataFrame
        Delay line data of one vintage.
    max_delay : int
        Longest delay shown.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        One panel per province with at least 10 cases, with the count,
        mean and median in the title.
    """
    counts = delays["location"].value_counts()
    locs = list(counts.index[counts >= 10])
    names = location_names(delays)
    fig, axes = panel_grid(len(locs), 3)
    colour = MODEL_COLOURS[mode][0]
    bins = list(np.arange(-0.5, max_delay + 1.5))
    for ax, loc in zip(axes, locs, strict=True):
        d = delays.loc[delays["location"] == loc, "delay"]
        ax.hist(d.clip(upper=max_delay), bins=bins, density=True, color=colour)
        ax.set_title(
            f"{names.get(loc, loc)}: n {len(d)}, mean {d.mean():.1f}, "
            f"median {d.median():.0f}"
        )
        ax.set_xlim(-1, max_delay + 1)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Share of cases")
    for ax in axes:
        ax.set_xlabel("Days from onset to report")
    return fig

def plot_renewal_delay(
    summary: pd.DataFrame,
    baseline: pd.DataFrame,
    names: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot the renewal models' learnt delay at their latest origin.

    Parameters
    ----------
    summary : pandas.DataFrame
        `delay-summary.csv` rows (`nowcastrenewal.forecaster.
        delay_summary` with `model`, `vintage` and `location`).
    baseline : pandas.DataFrame
        `baseline_share` at the same release, with the country as
        `NATIONAL` for the fits pooled over provinces.
    names : mapping, optional
        Location names by code.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        A row per fit, pooled over provinces. Left: the share of onsets
        in the last week reported by each day since onset, to the day
        before the longest delay, with randomwalknowcast's share for the
        same place. Right: the mean delay by onset week. Lines are medians
        and bands 90% intervals.
    """
    names = dict(names or {})
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    latest = summary.groupby("model")["vintage"].transform("max")
    rows = summary.loc[summary["vintage"] == latest]
    models = list(dict.fromkeys(rows["model"]))
    places = list(dict.fromkeys(rows["location"]))
    places.sort(key=lambda p: (p != "shared", names.get(p, p)))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        len(places),
        2,
        figsize=(7.2, 2.1 * len(places)),
        squeeze=False,
        layout="constrained",
    )
    last_day = int(pd.to_numeric(rows["x"], errors="coerce").max())
    for (left, right), place in zip(axes, places, strict=True):
        here = rows.loc[rows["location"] == place]
        fitted = list(dict.fromkeys(here["model"]))
        where = NATIONAL if place == "shared" else place
        title = "Shared delay" if place == "shared" else names.get(place, place)
        left.set_title(f"{title}: {', '.join(fitted)}", fontsize=8, loc="left")
        base = baseline.loc[baseline["location"] == where]
        left.plot(
            base["age"],
            base["share"],
            color=ink["data"],
            ls="--",
            lw=1,
            label="randomwalknowcast",
        )
        lines = []
        for model in fitted:
            fit = here.loc[here["model"] == model]
            colour = model_colour(model, models, mode)
            share = fit.loc[fit["quantity"] == "reported_share"]
            day = pd.to_numeric(share["x"])
            share = share.loc[day < last_day]
            day = day.loc[share.index]
            delay = fit.loc[fit["quantity"] == "mean_delay"]
            week = pd.to_datetime(delay["x"])
            for ax, x, q in ((left, day, share), (right, week, delay)):
                ax.fill_between(x, q["q5"], q["q95"], color=colour, alpha=0.12)
                lines.append((ax, x, q["q50"], colour, model))
        # Later models are drawn first and wider, so a line that coincides
        # with another stays visible under it.
        width = {m: 1.2 + 1.2 * i for i, m in enumerate(fitted)}
        for ax, x, y, colour, model in reversed(lines):
            ax.plot(x, y, color=colour, lw=width[model], label=model)
        left.set_ylim(0, 1)
        left.set_ylabel("Share reported")
        right.set_ylabel("Mean delay (days)")
        date_axis(right)
    axes[-1][0].set_xlabel("Days since onset, last onset week")
    vintage = ", ".join(sorted(rows["vintage"].astype(str).unique()))
    fig.suptitle(f"Fits at {vintage}", fontsize=9)
    handles: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        for h, label in zip(*ax.get_legend_handles_labels(), strict=True):
            handles.setdefault(label, h)
    fig.legend(
        list(handles.values()),
        list(handles),
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncol=len(handles),
        fontsize=7,
        frameon=False,
    )
    return fig

def incomplete_after(vintage: object, weeks: int) -> pd.Timestamp:
    """Return the date after which weeks are not completely reported.

    max_horizon: int | None = None,
    weeks_before: int = 10,
    ncol: int = 2,

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame

    locations : sequence of str
        Locations to show, one panel each.
    models : sequence of str, optional

    truth_vintage : str, optional

    max_horizon : int, optional

    ...     lambda mode: plot_location_grid(
    ...         forecasts, real, ["CD"], mode=mode
    ...     ),
    ...     "figures/grid.svg",
    ... )

        shown_data.append((vintage, "--", "Data at the origin"))

        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))

def plot_forecasts(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    location: str,
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    kind: str = "real",
    truth_vintage: str | None = None,
    weeks_before: int = 10,
    mode: str = "light",
    complete_after_weeks: int = 3,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot forecasts against data at the time and later data, by date.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `nowcasteval.backtest.run_forecasts`.
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows holding each forecast's vintage and the truth vintage.
    location : str
        Location to show.
    models : sequence of str, optional
        Models in registry order. Defaults to those in `forecasts`.
    kind : str
        Vintage kind to show.
    truth_vintage : str, optional
        Vintage drawn as later data. Defaults to the latest real vintage.
    weeks_before : int
        Weeks of data shown before each forecast.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    complete_after_weeks : int
        Weeks after which a week of the later data counts as complete.
        Later weeks are shaded and their points drawn hollow.

    Returns
    -------

        One panel per reference date: data at the time (dashed), later
        data (solid) and each model's sample trajectories, 50% and 90%
        intervals and median.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from nowcasteval.plots import plot_forecasts
    >>> fig = plot_forecasts(forecasts, real, "CD")  # from `run_forecasts`
    >>> fig.savefig("national.png")
    """
    fc = forecasts.loc[
        (forecasts["location"] == location) & (forecasts["kind"] == kind)
    ]
    models = list(models or fc["model"].unique())
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    truth_v = truth_vintage or real["vintage"].max()
    truth = real.loc[
        (real["vintage"] == truth_v) & (real["location"] == location)
    ]
    refs = sorted(fc["reference_date"].unique())
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    cut = incomplete_after(truth_v, complete_after_weeks)
    fig, axes = panel_grid(len(refs), 4, width=3.0, height=2.3)
    for ax, ref in zip(axes, refs, strict=True):
        top: list[float] = []
        f_ref = fc.loc[fc["reference_date"] == ref]
        vintage = f_ref["vintage"].iloc[0]
        start = pd.Timestamp(ref) - pd.Timedelta(weeks=weeks_before)
        end = pd.Timestamp(f_ref["target_end_date"].max())
        at_time = target.loc[
            (target["kind"] == kind)
            & (target["vintage"] == vintage)
            & (target["location"] == location)
        ]
        shown = [(truth, "-", f"Data {truth_v}")]
        if vintage != truth_v:
            shown.append((at_time, "--", "Data at the time"))
        for rows, style, lab in shown:
            x = pd.to_datetime(rows["target_end_date"])
            sel = (x >= start) & (x <= end)

            if style == "-":
                _plot_data(
                    ax,
                    x[sel],
                    rows["total"][sel],
                    cut,
                    ink["data"],
                    lab,
                    ls=style,
                    lw=1.2,
                )
                continue
            ax.plot(
                x[sel],
                rows["total"][sel],
                color=ink["data"],
                ls=style,
                lw=1.2,
                label=lab,
            )
        drawn = False
        for m in models:
            s = f_ref.loc[f_ref["model"] == m]
            if not s.empty:
                draw_forecast(
                    ax, s, model_colour(m, models, mode), model_dash(m), m
                )
                _fit_y(ax, s, top)

        if not drawn:
            ax.text(
                0.5,
                0.92,
                "No forecast from this origin",

                ha="center",
                fontsize=7,
                color=ink["muted"],
            )
        ax.axvline(
            mdates.date2num(pd.Timestamp(ref)),
            color=ink["muted"],
            lw=0.8,
            ls=":",
        )
        shade_incomplete(ax, cut, mode)
        ax.set_title(f"{location}, origin {vintage}")
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=4))
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Cases by onset week")
    legend_below(fig, axes[0])
    return fig

def comparison_colours(
    ours: Mapping[str, str],
    submitted: Mapping[str, str],
    teams: Sequence[str],
) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Return the light colour, dark colour and dash of each comparison series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ours : mapping of str to str
        Label of each of our main builds to its registry name.
    submitted : mapping of str to str
        Label of each of our submitted series to the registry name of the
        model it submits, whose colour it takes, dashed.
    teams : sequence of str
        Every hub team.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Label to its light colour, dark colour and SVG dash: our main
        builds in their `model_style`, our submitted series in their
        model's colour dashed, and the hub teams solid in the greys of
        `hub_styles`.
    """
    from nowcastutils.base import list_models

    registry = [s.name for s in list_models()]
    out = {lab: model_style(m, registry) for lab, m in ours.items()}
    out |= {
        lab: (*model_style(m, registry)[:2], DASHES["dashed"])
        for lab, m in submitted.items()
    }
    grey = {mode: hub_styles(teams, mode) for mode in ("light", "dark")}
    out |= {t: (grey["light"][t][0], grey["dark"][t][0], "") for t in teams}
    return out

def plot_hub_round(
    quantiles: pd.DataFrame,
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    reference_date: str,
    colours: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str, str]],
    locations: Sequence[str] = ("CD",),
    complete_after_weeks: int = 3,
    weeks_before: int = 8,
    mode: str = "light",
    shown: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot our and the hub teams' intervals for one round against the data.

    Our series are in the top row, in their `comparison_colours`, and the
    hub teams in the bottom row, in greys with a marker each. Colours and
    markers do not depend on the round.

    Parameters
    ----------
    quantiles : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `bdbvhub.compare.forecast_quantiles`,
        with every round, so a team keeps its style across rounds.
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows; the latest real vintage is drawn as data.
    reference_date : str
        The round.
    locations : sequence of str
        Locations to show, one column each, if any model forecast them.
    complete_after_weeks : int
        Weeks after which a week of the data counts as complete.
        Later weeks are shaded and their points drawn hollow.
    weeks_before : int
        Weeks of data shown before the reference date.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    colours : mapping of str to (str, str, str)
        Our series' labels (`comparison_label`) to their light
        colour, dark colour and dash, in the order drawn. Every series of
        ours in the round needs one.
    shown : sequence of str, optional
        Labels of our series to draw. Defaults to all of ours in the
        round.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Per week and model, the median (point), 50% interval (thick line)
        and 90% interval (thin line), side by side, over the latest release,
        with the legend below the panels.
    """
    styles = hub_styles(
        sorted(set(quantiles.loc[quantiles["source"] == "hub", "model"])), mode
    )
    q = quantiles.loc[quantiles["reference_date"].astype(str) == reference_date]
    q = q.assign(
        label=[
            comparison_label(m, s)
            for m, s in zip(q["model"], q["source"], strict=True)
        ]
    )
    hub = q["source"] == "hub"
    if shown is not None:
        q = q.loc[hub | q["label"].isin(list(shown))]
        hub = q["source"] == "hub"
    here = set(q.loc[~hub, "label"])
    pick = 0 if mode == "light" else 1
    rows = [
        {
            lab: (c[pick], "o", c[2])
            for lab, c in colours.items()
            if lab in here
        },
        {lab: (*styles[lab], "") for lab in sorted(set(q.loc[hub, "label"]))},
    ]
    locs = [loc for loc in locations if loc in set(q["location"])]
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    latest = real["vintage"].max()
    names = location_names(real)
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    cut = incomplete_after(latest, complete_after_weeks)
    n_col = max(len(locs), 1)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        2,
        n_col,
        figsize=(4.0 * n_col, 5.6),
        squeeze=False,
        sharex=True,
        sharey="col",
        layout="constrained",
    )
    ref = pd.Timestamp(reference_date)
    start = ref - pd.Timedelta(weeks=weeks_before)
    for j, loc in enumerate(locs):
        ql = q.loc[q["location"] == loc]
        data = real.loc[(real["vintage"] == latest) & (real["location"] == loc)]
        x = pd.to_datetime(data["target_end_date"])
        end = pd.to_datetime(ql["target_end_date"]).max()
        sel = (x >= start) & (x <= end)
        for i, (ax, style) in enumerate(zip(axes[:, j], rows, strict=True)):
            _plot_data(
                ax,
                x[sel],
                data["total"][sel],
                cut,
                ink["data"],
                f"Data {latest}",
                lw=1.2,
                zorder=3,
            )
            width = 5.0 / max(len(style), 1)
            for k, (lab, (colour, marker, dash)) in enumerate(style.items()):
                m = ql.loc[ql["label"] == lab]
                offset = pd.Timedelta(days=(k - (len(style) - 1) / 2) * width)
                xm = pd.to_datetime(m["target_end_date"]) + offset
                ls = mpl_dash(dash)
                ax.vlines(
                    xm, m["q05"], m["q95"], color=colour, lw=1, alpha=0.7, ls=ls
                )
                ax.vlines(xm, m["q25"], m["q75"], color=colour, lw=3, ls=ls)
                ax.plot(
                    xm,
                    m["q50"],
                    marker,
                    ms=4,
                    ls="",
                    label=lab,
                    **point_style(colour, dash),
                )
            ax.axvline(mdates.date2num(ref), color=ink["muted"], lw=0.8, ls=":")
            shade_incomplete(ax, cut, mode)
            title = ("Ours", "Hub teams")[i]
            ax.set_title(f"{names.get(loc, loc)} ({loc}): {title}", fontsize=9)
            ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.AutoDateLocator(maxticks=5))
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        ax.set_ylabel("Confirmed cases by onset week")
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        for h, lab in zip(*ax.get_legend_handles_labels(), strict=True):
            seen.setdefault(lab, h)
    fig.legend(
        list(seen.values()),
        list(seen),
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncol=min(len(seen), 4),
        fontsize=7,
        frameon=False,
    )
    return fig

def plot_scores(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    by: str = "horizon",
    metric: str = "crps",
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "light",
    colours: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None,
    baseline: str | None = None,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot mean scores by horizon or location, one panel per vintage kind.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `score_forecasts`.
    by : str
        `"horizon"` or `"location"`.
    metric : str
        A score column, such as `"crps"`, `"log_crps"`, `"coverage_90"` or
        `"bias"`.
    models : sequence of str, optional
        Models in registry order.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    colours : mapping of str to (str, str, str), optional
        Model to its light colour, dark colour and dash. Defaults to
        `model_style`.

    baseline : str, optional
        The model relative metrics are relative to, named in the axis
        label; needed for a `relative_` metric.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Mean score by `by`, with the number of forecasts in the title.
    """
    models = list(models or scores["model"].unique())
    kinds = [k for k in ("real", "simulated") if k in set(scores["kind"])]
    fig, axes = panel_grid(len(kinds), 3, width=3.6, height=2.6)
    for ax, kind in zip(axes, kinds, strict=True):
        s = scores.loc[scores["kind"] == kind]
        mean = s.groupby(["model", by])[metric].mean().unstack(0)
        if by == "location":
            order = s.groupby("location")["truth"].sum().sort_values()

    quantiles: pd.DataFrame,
    releases: pd.DataFrame,
    locations: Sequence[str],
    models: Sequence[str],
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot each model's final forecast of the recent weeks by origin.

    Parameters
    ----------
    quantiles : pandas.DataFrame
        `evaluation.nowcast.ReleaseBacktest.quantiles`.
    releases : pandas.DataFrame
        Real target rows with `vintage`, `location`, `target_end_date`
        and `total`.

    models : sequence of str

    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        One panel per origin and place. Lines are the counts each release
        reports, bars the 50% and 90% intervals.
    """
    final = quantiles.loc[quantiles["target"] == "complete"]
    final = final.loc[final["model"].isin(models)]
    origins = sorted(final["origin"].unique())
    fig, axes = panel_grid(
        len(origins) * len(locations), len(locations), width=3.4, height=2.6
    )
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    shades = np.linspace(0.4, 1.0, len(releases["vintage"].unique()))
    # Each model's bars sit side by side within the week.
    width, mid = 5.6 / len(models), (len(models) - 1) / 2
    for i, origin in enumerate(origins):
        for j, loc in enumerate(locations):
            ax = axes[i * len(locations) + j]
            weeks = final.loc[
                (final["origin"] == origin) & (final["location"] == loc)
            ]["target_end_date"]
            lo = pd.Timestamp(weeks.min()) - pd.Timedelta(days=7)
            for v, a in zip(
                sorted(releases["vintage"].unique()), shades, strict=True
            ):
                r = releases.loc[
                    (releases["vintage"] == v) & (releases["location"] == loc)
                ]
                x = pd.to_datetime(r["target_end_date"])
                keep = (x >= lo) & (x <= pd.Timestamp(origin) + pd.Timedelta(7))
                ax.plot(
                    x[keep],
                    r["total"][keep],
                    color=ink["data"],
                    alpha=a,
                    lw=1.2,
                    label=f"Release {v}",
                )
            for m_i, m in enumerate(models):
                rows = final.loc[
                    (final["origin"] == origin)
                    & (final["location"] == loc)
                    & (final["model"] == m)

                colour = model_colour(m, models, mode)
                _draw_bars(ax, rows, colour, model_dash(m), (m_i - mid) * width)
            ax.set_title(f"{loc}, origin {origin}")

        labels.append(f"{m} (50% and 90%)")
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        labels,
        fontsize=7,

        ncols=min(len(labels), 5),

def plot_truth_changes(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    names: Mapping[str, str],
    weeks: int = 16,
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot each place's weekly counts in every release and their changes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Real target rows with every release.
    names : mapping of str to str
        Place names by id.
    weeks : int
        Weeks shown, up to the latest release's last week.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Per place with cases in the weeks shown, most first, the count by
        onset week with one line per release,
        from the oldest (faint) to the newest (strong), and under it the
        change from the previous release by week, with a line at 0.
    """
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    releases = sorted(set(real["vintage"]))
    shades = np.linspace(0.3, 1.0, len(releases))
    # Newer releases are stronger: darker on light, lighter on dark.
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("Blues")
    colours = [cmap(v if mode == "light" else 1.25 - v) for v in shades]
    end = pd.to_datetime(real["target_end_date"]).max()
    start = end - pd.Timedelta(weeks=weeks)
    wide = real.assign(
        target_end_date=pd.to_datetime(real["target_end_date"])
    ).pivot_table(
        index=["location", "target_end_date"],
        columns="vintage",
        values="total",
    )
    recent = wide.loc[wide.index.get_level_values(1) > start]
    latest = recent[releases[-1]].groupby(level=0).sum()
    latest = latest.loc[latest > 0].sort_values(ascending=False, kind="stable")
    locations = list(latest.index)
    ncol = min(4, len(locations))
    nrow = int(np.ceil(len(locations) / ncol))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        2 * nrow,
        ncol,
        figsize=(3.4 * ncol, 3.6 * nrow),
        squeeze=False,
        layout="constrained",
        gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1] * nrow},
    )
    for k in range(nrow * ncol):
        row, col = 2 * (k // ncol), k % ncol
        top, low = axes[row, col], axes[row + 1, col]
        if k >= len(locations):
            top.set_visible(False)
            low.set_visible(False)
            continue
        loc = locations[k]
        rows = wide.loc[loc]
        rows = rows.loc[rows.index > start]
        change = rows.diff(axis=1)
        for i, vin in enumerate(releases):
            top.plot(
                rows.index, rows[vin], color=colours[i], lw=1.4, label=str(vin)
            )
            if i:
                low.plot(rows.index, change[vin], color=colours[i], lw=1.2)
        low.axhline(0, color=ink["muted"], lw=1, ls=":")
        top.set_title(names.get(loc, loc), fontsize=9)
        top.set_xticklabels([])
        for ax in (top, low):
            ax.set_xlim(start, end + pd.Timedelta(days=3))
            ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator())
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b"))
        if k % ncol == 0:
            top.set_ylabel("Count by onset week")
            low.set_ylabel("Change")
    handles, labels = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        labels,
        title="Release",
        fontsize=7,
        title_fontsize=8,
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncols=len(releases),
    )
    return fig

    """Wrap a Markdown table in a searchable, sortable block.

        'markdown="1">\n\n'
        f"{table.strip()}\n\n"
        "</div>\n"

Per-forecast scores for the in-browser summaries.

The page embeds one row per model, origin, release, place and week, and docs/javascripts/summarise.js summarises a selection of them as relative_crps does: the mean of each metric over each model's own forecasts and, for relative metrics, its pairwise relative skill (nowcasteval.scoring.pairwise_skill). The skill is computed here, once, as each model's geometric mean of ratios (skill) for every selection the page offers: each round or all rounds, by scale or by place, overall or at each horizon. The page divides one model's by the chosen baseline's, which only rescales them. A model with fewer forecasts than the baseline is marked partial (mark_partial). A new metric is a score column and a label.

def mark_partial(
    table: pd.DataFrame, by: Sequence[str], baseline: str
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mark the rows of models that lack some of the baseline's cells.

    Relative scores are on the forecasts the baseline also made, so `n`
    of a model with every one of the baseline's cells is the baseline's,
    and those rows can be read side by side. A model with fewer is
    partial: its scores are on other forecasts and are read apart.

    Parameters
    ----------
    table : pandas.DataFrame
        `relative_crps` or `relative_energy` output, with `model`, the `by`
        columns and `n` (or `n_energy`).
    by : sequence of str
        Columns of a row other than `model`.
    baseline : str
        The baseline of `table`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        `table` with `cells`, the baseline's n in the row's group, and
        `partial`, whether the model has fewer.
    """
    n = "n" if "n" in table.columns else "n_energy"
    by = [c for c in by if c in table.columns]
    base = table.loc[table["model"] == baseline, [*by, n]]
    base = base.rename(columns={n: "cells"})
    out = (
        table.merge(base, on=by, how="left")
        if by
        else table.assign(cells=base["cells"].iloc[0] if len(base) else None)
    )
    out["partial"] = (out[n] < out["cells"]).fillna(False).astype(bool)
    return out

def summary_rows(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    models: Sequence[str],
    colours: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str, str]],
    names: Mapping[str, str],
    baseline: str,
    metrics: Sequence[tuple[str, str, float | None, bool]] = SUMMARY_METRICS,
    default_on: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    energy: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    pool_of: Callable[[str], str] = _pool,
    pool_labels: Mapping[str, str] = _POOLS,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return the per-forecast rows and their labels for one target.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        One row per forecast scored against one release, with `model`,
        `origin`, `truth_vintage`, `location`, `target_end_date`,
        `horizon` (weeks from the reference date) and the metric columns.
    models : sequence of str
        Models in order. Rows of other models are left out.
    colours : mapping of str to (str, str, str)
        Model to its light colour, dark colour and dash.
    names : mapping of str to str
        Place names by id. Zones not named show their code.
    baseline : str
        The model relative metrics divide by.
    metrics : sequence of (str, str, float or None, bool)
        As `SUMMARY_METRICS`.
    default_on : sequence of str, optional
        Models ticked at first. Defaults to all.
    energy : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        Energy scores (`energy_scores`) with `model`, `origin`,
        `truth_vintage`, `scale` and the `ENERGY_SUMMARY` columns.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `models` (name, light and dark colour, dash, ticked at first),
        `baseline` (its index), `metrics` (key, label, ref, relative),
        `origins`, `releases`, `weeks`, `pools` (id and label, in order),
        `places` (id, name, pool) and `rows`: model, origin, release,
        place and week indices, then each metric, `horizons`, each row's
        horizon, and `skill` (`_skill`). With `energy`, also `energy`:
        `metrics` (key and label) and `rows` of model, origin, release and
        pool indices, then each energy score.
    """
    shown = [m for m in models if m in set(scores["model"])]
    s = scores.loc[scores["model"].isin(shown)]
    origins = sorted(set(s["origin"].astype(str)))
    releases = sorted(set(s["truth_vintage"].astype(str)))
    weeks = sorted(set(s["target_end_date"].astype(str)))
    pools = [p for p in pool_labels if p in set(s["location"].map(pool_of))]
    places = sorted(
        set(s["location"]),
        key=lambda x: (pools.index(pool_of(x)), names.get(x, x)),
    )
    on = set(shown if default_on is None else default_on)
    keys = [m[0] for m in metrics]
    idx = {
        "model": {m: i for i, m in enumerate(shown)},
        "origin": {o: i for i, o in enumerate(origins)},
        "truth_vintage": {r: i for i, r in enumerate(releases)},
        "location": {p: i for i, p in enumerate(places)},
        "target_end_date": {w: i for i, w in enumerate(weeks)},
    }
    cols = s[[*idx, *keys]].astype(dict.fromkeys(idx, str))
    horizons = [int(h) for h in s["horizon"]]
    rows = [
        [
            *(idx[c][v] for c, v in zip(idx, r[: len(idx)], strict=True)),
            *(round(float(v), 6) for v in r[len(idx) :]),
        ]
        for r in cols.itertuples(index=False)
    ]
    out: dict[str, object] = {
        "models": [
            {
                "name": m,
                "light": colours[m][0],
                "dark": colours[m][1],
                "dash": colours[m][2],
                "on": m in on,
            }
            for m in shown
        ],
        "baseline": shown.index(baseline),
        "metrics": [
            {"key": k, "label": label, "ref": ref, "relative": rel}
            for k, label, ref, rel in metrics
        ],
        "origins": origins,
        "releases": releases,
        "weeks": weeks,
        "pools": [{"id": p, "label": pool_labels[p]} for p in pools],
        "places": [
            {"id": p, "name": names.get(p, p), "pool": pool_of(p)}
            for p in places
        ],
        "rows": rows,
        "horizons": horizons,
        "skill": _skill(
            s,
            shown,
            baseline,
            idx,
            pools,
            pool_of,
            [k for k, _, _, rel in metrics if rel],
        ),
    }
    if energy is not None:
        out["energy"] = _energy_rows(energy, idx, pools)
    return out

def summary_html(
    srcs: Mapping[str, str],
    title: str,
    view: str = "overall",
    static: str | None = None,
    map_src: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Return the page element `docs/javascripts/scoresummary.js` fills.

    Parameters
    ----------
    srcs : mapping of str to str
        URL of each target's `summary_rows` JSON, relative to the page
        (`targets_attr`).
    title : str
        Accessible name of the summary.
    view : str
        `"overall"` for one group of bars for the chosen scale, `"place"`
        for one group per place and a place picker, or `"horizon"` for a
        line per model by horizon.
    static : str, optional
        Path of a static SVG, relative to the page, shown without
        JavaScript. Its `-dark` twin is shown in the dark theme.
    map_src : str, optional
        URL of the health zone GeoJSON, relative to the page. The place
        view then offers a map of the metric shown.
    """
    fallback = "The interactive summary needs JavaScript."
    if static is not None:
        dark = static.removesuffix(".svg") + "-dark.svg"
        fallback = (
            f'<img src="{static}#only-light" alt="{title}">'
            f'<img src="{dark}#only-dark" alt="{title}">'
        )
    shown = "" if map_src is None else f' data-map="{map_src}"'
    return (
        f'<div class="scoresummary"{targets_attr(srcs)} data-view="{view}"'
        f"{shown} "
        f'role="group" aria-label="{title}">\n'
        f"<noscript>{fallback}</noscript>\n"
        "</div>\n"
    )
